24	Caption-level agreement with the original paper runs:
25	- MSR-VTT: 2935 / 2990 predictions identical (98.2%)
26	- MSVD: 662 / 670 predictions identical (98.8%)
27	
28	The residual differences are fp16 / beam-search tie-breaking nondeterminism
29	(torch 2.1.2 vs the original 2.1.0); all metrics agree to within 0.03.
30	
31	## Setup
32	
33	- MSR-VTT: checkpoint `train_evcap_top7_..._prompt5_review.pt`, topn=7,
34	  `datasets/MSRVTT-v2/test_16frames.yaml`, 16 frames, beam width 5, seed 42.
35	- MSVD: checkpoint `train_evcap_top3_..._prompt5_msvd.pt`, topn=3,
36	  `datasets/MSVD/test_16frames.yaml` (670 test videos), 16 frames, beam width 5,
37	  seed 42.
38	- Backbone: EVA-ViT-G (frozen) + BLIP-2 Q-Former + Video-LLaMA-initialized video
39	  Q-Former + Vicuna-7B-v1.3 (frozen), fp16, bs 1, single RTX A6000.
40	
41	## Files
42	
43	- Runner scripts: `run_msrvtt.sh`, `run_msvd_test.sh`
44	  (plus `run_msvd.sh`, the train-split sanity check)
45	- Logs: `logs/repro_msrvtt.log`, `logs/cocoeval_msrvtt.log`,
46	  `logs/repro_msvd_test.log`
47	- Generated captions / metrics:
48	  - `lj/EVCapCode/outputs/eval_repro_msrvtt/`
49	  - `lj/EVCapCode/outputs/old/eval_repro_msvd_test/`
50	  - train-split sanity check: `lj/EVCapCode/outputs/old/eval_repro_msvd/`
51	
52	## Issues found and fixed
53	
54	1. `datasets` was a broken symlink to `/mnt/data/lj/datasets`; repointed to
55	   `.../xyl/Display/lj/datasets`.
56	2. `repo_type='lmsys'` was passed to `LlamaForCausalLM.from_pretrained`, which
57	   transformers 4.28 forwards to the model constructor and crashes
58	   (`unexpected keyword argument 'repo_type'`). Removed in both EVCap model
59	   files; irrelevant for local paths.
60	3. Missing deps in the venv: `progressbar`, `future`, `ete3`, `deprecated`,
61	   `easydict`, `ipdb`, `accelerate==0.16.0`, `datasets==2.14.6`,
62	   `pyarrow==14.0.0`, `huggingface_hub==0.18.0`.
63	4. SPICE was broken twice in `evaluation/pycocoevalcap/spice/spice.py`:
64	   `-Xmx32G` was placed after `-jar` (Java treats it as the jar name), and
65	   Java 21 blocks FST reflection. Fixed the argument order and pinned
66	   `/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/bin/java`; SPICE now reproduces the
67	   reference values (MSR-VTT 8.58 vs 8.59, MSVD 8.78 vs 8.78).
68	5. `datasets/MSVD/train_16frames.yaml` is the **training split** (1200 videos).
69	   Evaluating there yields inflated scores (BLEU-1 98.8) because the model saw
70	   those videos. The paper's MSVD numbers correspond to
71	   `test_16frames.yaml` (670 videos). The repo's own June-19 script generated
72	   `..._msvdtrain_generated_captions.json` but its cocoeval step pointed at the
73	   stale `..._msvd_generated_captions.json` (the 670-video test predictions), so
74	   the published metrics were effectively computed on the test split.

86	the two evaluations and restarted afterwards; restart command:

#!/bin/bash
set -e
ROOT=/media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1/xyl/Display
REPRO=$ROOT/repro_evcap
cd $ROOT/lj/EVCapCode

export TORCH_HOME=$REPRO/torch_cache
export HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE=$REPRO/hf_cache
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export USE_TF=0
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
PY=$REPRO/venv/bin/python

FILE_NAME=top3_bs1_load_video_feature_sim_score_cross_fusion_gate_not_share_linear_prompt5_msvd
OUT=outputs/old/eval_repro_msvd_test

$PY -u eval_evcap_fix_video_llama_xclip_msrvtt_fusion_gate_prompt5_msvd.py \
  --device cuda:0 \
  --test_yaml datasets/MSVD/test_16frames.yaml \
  --out_path $OUT \
  --ckpt_name train_evcap_${FILE_NAME}.pt \
  --bs 1 --epochs 1 --topn 3 --random_seed 42 --max_num_frames 16 \
  --num_video_query_token 32 --freeze_video_qformer True \
  --load_video_feature True --retriever True \
  --ext_path ext_data/msvd_rerank_sentence_by_sentence_as_inference_rouge_quality_with_video_ids.json \
  --prompt_path prompts/prompt_evcap_msrvtt_detail_smallcap_prompt5.txt \
  --llm_model $REPRO/models/vicuna-7b-v1.3

$PY evaluation/cocoeval.py \
  --result_file_path $OUT/eval_evcap_${FILE_NAME}_generated_captions.json \
  --eval_file $OUT/eval_evcap_${FILE_NAME}.json

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description:

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

system.text: You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.

You are an agent working with the user toward their goals, using your own judgment along the way.

IMPORTANT: Assist with authorized security testing, defensive security, CTF challenges, and educational contexts. Refuse requests for destructive techniques, DoS attacks, mass targeting, supply chain compromise, or detection evasion for malicious purposes. Dual-use security tools (C2 frameworks, credential testing, exploit development) require clear authorization context: pentesting engagements, CTF competitions, security research, or defensive use cases.

# Harness
 - Text you output outside of tool use is displayed to the user as Github-flavored markdown in a terminal.
 - Tools run behind a user-selected permission mode; a denied call means the user declined it — adjust, don't retry verbatim.
 - The system may send updates, reminders, or modifications to rules via mid-conversation system turns. These are system-controlled, unlike function results. Hooks may intercept tool calls; treat hook output as user feedback.
 - Prefer the dedicated file/search tools over shell commands when one fits. Independent tool calls can run in parallel in one response.
 - Reference code as `file_path:line_number` — it's clickable.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

## 二、各表状态（刚核对完）

| 表 | 内容 | 状态 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Table 1 | SOTA 主结果 | ✅ 本人重跑 | MSR-VTT 86.69/50.11/32.47/66.64/72.20；MSVD 91.53/69.67/47.04/84.04/158.32；字幕级一致率 98.2%/98.8% |

## 结论先行

**下载任务未启动，0 个视频，也未在任何系统盘路径留下任何数据。** 原因有两个，其中任何一个单独就足以让任务失败：

1. 目标盘 `/dev/sda` 当前以 **只读** 方式挂载，无法创建 `Panda-2M/` 目录；
2. 即使恢复可写，**本机访问不了 YouTube**，而 Panda-2M 只提供元数据（YouTube 链接 + 时间戳 + 字幕），真实片段必须逐条抓取。

我只做了只读诊断，没有执行 remount、umount、fsck、重启或任何写操作，UK-law 任务（PID 491379/491592）未受影响。

---

## 1. 目标目录归属确认 ✅

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 指定路径 | `/media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1/xyl/Panda-2M/`（目录尚不存在） |
| 设备 | `/dev/sda`（不是根分区） |
| 型号 | `ST8000NM017B-2TJ`，8.00 TB SATA HDD |
| 文件系统 | ext4，UUID `37b77782-...` |
| 已用 / 可用 | 3.1 TB / **3.86 TiB（4.24 TB，4,238,557,659,136 字节）** |

容量核算：1.6 TB 数据集写入后占约 42%，仍余 ~2.2 TiB。空间没问题。

## 2. 当前挂载状态 ⚠️

同一文件系统被挂载了 **两次，都是只读**：

```
/dev/sda  /mnt/rag-check                                  ext4  ro,relatime,norecovery
/dev/sda  /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1  ext4  ro,relatime,norecovery
```

`/etc/fstab` 当前行：

```
UUID=37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1  /media/bn/...  ext4  ro,noload,nofail  0 0
```

## 3. 只读原因调查（纯只读诊断）

时间线是从 systemd journal / sudo 日志 / fstab 备份还原出来的，证据链完整：

| 时间 | 事件 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-10-23 之前 | 该盘**不在 fstab 里**（手动挂载） | `/etc/fstab.bak.20261101-103946` 无此行 |
| 2026-11-01 10:39 | 加入 fstab：**`defaults,nofail 0 2`**（正常读写 + fsck） | `/etc/fstab.backup.20261107174449` |
| 2026-11-06 19:59:47 | 开机，内核识别 sda：`Write Protect is off` | `journalctl -k` |
| 2026-11-06 20:01:17 | systemd 等待 `dev-disk-by-uuid-37b77782...` **超时**，mount 单元与 fsck 单元 dependency 失败 | journal |
| 2026-11-06 20:57:37 | **bn 手动执行 `sudo mount -o ro,noload UUID=... /mnt/rag-check`** | sudo 审计行 + 内核 `EXT4-fs (sda): mounted ... ro without journal` |
| 2026-11-07 17:44:49 | fstab 被改成 **`ro,noload,nofail 0 0`**，同时留了备份 | fstab mtime + 备份文件 |
| 至今 | `/media/...` 由 systemd 按 fstab 以 ro 挂载 | mount 单元 active |

**判断：只读是人为配置的保护性挂载，不是内核因文件系统错误自动 remount-ro。**

- 两个 boot 的内核日志里 **没有任何** `EXT4-fs error`、`I/O error`、`ata*.error`、`medium error`、`SCSI reset`；
- 没有任何 fsck 在该盘上跑过的记录（systemd-fsck 单元在 20:01 因设备超时就失败了）。

**但必须说清楚的不确定性**：`noload` 意味着日志从未被回放，文件系统是否“干净”无法通过日志确认；`/dev/sda` 是 `660 root:disk`，我不在 disk 组，`smartctl` / `tune2fs -l` / `dumpe2fs` 全部需要 root，因此 **SMART 健康度和超级块里的 `s_last_fsck`/`state` 都还没验证**。

## 4. 恢复写入需要什么，以及为什么现在不能做

**硬阻塞：正在跑的 UK-law 任务直接从这块盘映射了文件。**

```
pid 491379 (python, UK-law)  mmap /media/.../xyl/Jnh_rag/.venv_rag_vllm/.../*.so
pid 491592 (VLLM::EngineCore) 同样 mmap 同一批 .so
另有 6 个 bash/claude 会话 cwd 在该盘内，nautilus(6638) 持有 fd
```

后果：`umount` 会因 EBUSY 失败；而 `umount -l`/强行卸载会破坏正在运行的 GPU 任务——这是你明确禁止的。加上 `fuser -vm` 已确认这一点，不是猜测。

两条路，都需要你的 sudo 密码 + 明确授权：

**方案 A（最轻，不中断 UK-law，但可能被内核拒绝）**

```bash
# 先做只读检查，判断日志是否干净
sudo tune2fs -l /dev/sda | grep -E 'Filesystem state|Last checked|Last mount|Journal'
sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda | tail -30

# 在线 remount，不卸载、不影响 mmap 的进程
sudo mount -o remount,rw /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1
```

- 优点：零中断，失败也无副作用，可立刻 `remount,ro` 回退；
- 风险点：`noload` 挂载的文件系统，ext4 内核很可能拒绝 ro→rw（日志未加载）；若 `Filesystem state` 不是 `clean`，**不应**走这条路。

**方案 B（规范做法，需要 UK-law 结束后或你同意停它）**

```bash
# 1. 所有 cwd 在盘内的 shell/claude/nautilus 先退出去
# 2. 等 UK-law 任务结束（预计 11-09 下午~傍晚）或你决定停它
sudo umount /mnt/rag-check
sudo umount /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1
# 3. 离线体检（7.3T HDD，预计 20~60 分钟，可能更久）
sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda
sudo fsck.ext4 -f -y /dev/sda
# 4. 读写挂载
sudo mount -o rw /dev/sda /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1
# 5. 恢复 fstab（否则重启又变回 ro）
sudo cp /etc/fstab.backup.20261107174449 /etc/fstab
```

**前提条件清单**：① sudo 密码；② 你明确授权选 A 还是 B；③ 若选 B，UK-law 任务让路的时机；④ `fsck` 报告无异常（若有错误，先备份再决定）。

## 5. 下载可行性（这是第二个、你可能还不知道的阻塞点）

数据集本身：2.4M 片段 / 1.6 TB / 元数据 CSV 约 118 MB，对应 **Panda-70M 的 Training (2M) split**（Snap Research，CVPR 2024）；另有一个整理版 `Zhuzhenxin/Panda-2M`（同样只有 YouTube 链接 + 时间戳 + 字幕，不含视频）。

`yt-dlp` 和 `ffmpeg` 也都没装（可经清华 pip 镜像安装，纯 CPU）。

**结论：恢复可写 ≠ 能下载。** 需要你提供以下之一：YouTube 代理/VPN 的地址与端口；或一个已有视频文件的镜像源（ModelScope / OpenDataLab / 校内存储）；或告知你手上已有的数据来源。

按 HDD 顺序写 ~150–200 MB/s、YouTube 抓取实际受网络限制估算，1.6 TB 大约需要 20 小时（20 MB/s）到 4 天（5 MB/s）。

| 项目 | 状态 |

| 目标盘挂载 | `ro,relatime,norecovery`（两处挂载点均只读） |

===== RELAY_README =====
# Overnight GPU relay — deployment notes

## Scope
Runs the remaining Benchmark 3000 matrix after the 40,995 gpt-oss-20b inferences:

| item | value |
|---|---|
| conditions | O3, SYSTEM_CLEAN, ORACLE_CLEAN, MATCHED, SHUFFLED (5) |
| seeds | 53, 71, 97 |
| cases | all 2,733 binary-valid cases |
| tasks per model | **40,995** |

`MISSING` is deliberately excluded: its gold label is `ablated_oracle_decision`
(the counterfactual Oracle re-run), while the frozen runner scores against the
base-case gold. Running it would produce uninterpretable numbers.

## Queue (priority order)
1. `qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507-fp8` — 3B-active MoE, high throughput
2. `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` — dense, resumes from its checkpoint
3. `qwen3.5-27b-fp8`
4. `qwen2.5-7b-instruct`
5. `qwen3.5-35b-a3b-fp8` — **EXCLUDED 2026-11-08 13:12 CST**: under the frozen
   protocol (enable_thinking, max_tokens 4096) it spends the whole budget in the thinking
   channel; 28/32 rows failed and only 2/32 carried a usable final answer. Sealed as
   PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE; see `runs/sealed/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE_*`.
   Do not re-queue it under the same protocol.
6. `qwen3-32b-fp8` (reserve)

**Reorder 2026-11-08 03:00 CST.** Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (dense, 27B) was started first and
measured 15–32 items/min over its first ~10 min (96 rows), i.e. 21–45 h for one
40,995-task matrix — it cannot finish overnight. It was checkpointed (96 rows kept)
and moved to slot 2 so the fast MoE can complete a full 5×3 matrix inside the
window. No inference results were discarded and no stack parameter changed.
Thermal stop raised 88 → 90 °C (A6000 throttles ~93 °C; steady state was 87 °C, inside
the old band, which risked cooldown churn), resume 80 → 82 °C.

Reserve table: `logs/task_reserve.json` (conservative lower bounds, ≥12 h required;
live rate and ETA replace the estimates in `logs/relay_status.json`).

## Inference stack
Frozen 34d40672 pipeline (`runner.py`, `prompt_adapter.py`, `evaluator.py`) — the same
prompts, evaluator and decoding used for the 40,995 gpt-oss inferences. Only
scheduling is new. `runner.py` gained three environment overrides used by the relay
tiers; defaults are unchanged (`0.90 / 64 / 32768`).

## Safety / recovery behaviour
- Single instance: `flock` on `logs/relay.lock` + `logs/relay.pid`; a second relay exits 3.
- Never preempts: waits until `nvidia-smi` reports zero compute apps, <1 GiB used, <5% util.
  Any nvidia-smi failure is fail-closed (treated as busy).
- Missing weights: `SKIPPED_MISSING_WEIGHTS`, advances immediately.
- OOM (`out of memory`, `no available memory for the cache blocks`, …): exactly one lower tier.
- Non-OOM child exit: recorded `exit_code`, no OOM-tier sweep, one same-tier resume only when
  `rc=0` and keys are still missing, then advance the queue.
- Thermal: two consecutive samples ≥88 °C → terminate child, cool to ≤80 °C, resume from
  the checkpoint at the same tier.
- Resume: every run_key is `case|condition|seed`; the runner skips completed keys on restart.
  Relay relaunch skips complete models (`ALREADY_COMPLETE`).
- `phase=COMPLETED` only when every queued model's 40,995 keys are present.
- **Known evidence caveat**: on a checkpointed resume the `real_inference_confirmed`
  event fires from the pre-existing rows in the output file, not from a row generated by
  the new process. Treat it as "output non-empty", and confirm new inference by a row
  count increase or a `generated_at` later than the launch time.
- **Rate meter caveat**: the relay samples over 60 s. For slow bursty models (dense 27B
  emits a 32-row batch every 85–180 s) a 60 s window often sees zero, so
  `rate_per_min`/`eta_min` read null. Use a ≥10-minute window
  (`logs/dense_rate_10min.txt`) for those models.
- Historical gpt-oss audit is **decoupled**: a FAIL writes
  `logs/ALARM_historical_audit.json` and is never auto-certified, but it does not block
  the queue.

## Launchers
```bash
cd /home/bn/uklaw3000_run_20261108
setsid nohup python -u overnight_relay.py >> logs/relay_run.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
python relay_report.py            # live evidence snapshot
```
Monitor: `logs/relay_status.json`, `logs/relay_events.jsonl`,
`logs/runner_<tag>_tier<N>.log`, outputs under `runs/overnight/<tag>/`.

## CPU fault injection (all pass, no GPU used)
`python relay_selftest.py` → 8/8:
missing weights skip · non-OOM no 3-tier retry · OOM single tier fallback ·
rc=0 resume · already-complete skip · no premature COMPLETED · single-instance lock ·
≥12 h reserve.

## Provenance caveats
- This run root is an extracted snapshot of commit
  `34d406724803d92c417582f60ff9652e2a8be354`; there is no `.git`, so runner manifests
  record `UNKNOWN_GIT_COMMIT`. `PROVENANCE.json` is authoritative.
- Historical gpt-oss rows predate the `git_commit`/`prompt_config_hash` per-row fields

- Benchmark 3000 results must never be pooled with Frozen-89.

- Single instance: `flock` on `logs/relay.lock` + `logs/relay.pid`; a second relay exits 3.

## 4. 离线 fsck 的安全流程（待你执行，我未执行）

前提：关闭上表 3 个 GNOME 终端标签页（pts/0、pts/1、pts/3）与 Nautilus（**这会关闭本 Claude 会话**），再新开一个终端（cwd 在 `/home`）。

```bash
# 0. 确认无占用（应只剩 kernel /mnt/rag-check）
fuser -vm /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1
fuser -vm /mnt/rag-check

# 1. 卸载两个挂载点
sudo umount /mnt/rag-check
sudo umount /media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1

# 2. 只读健康检查（不写盘）
sudo apt-get install -y smartmontools        # 当前未安装
sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda | tail -40          # 重点：Reallocated_Sector_Ct / Pending / UDMA_CRC
sudo tune2fs -l /dev/sda | grep -E 'Filesystem state|Last checked|Last mount|Errors behavior|Journal'
sudo dumpe2fs -h /dev/sda | head -40

# 3. 只读 fsck（关键：-n = 只检查、全部回答 no，不修复）
sudo fsck.ext4 -n -f /dev/sda
```

说明：
- `-n` 只报告、不修改；7.3 TB HDD 预计 **20–60 分钟或更久**。
- 若报告“clean”，再执行 `sudo mount -o rw /dev/sda /media/...`；若报告错误，**先停**，把输出发我，再决定 `-p` 还是人工 `e2fsck -f` 逐项确认——不会自动 `-y`。
- 恢复读写后把 fstab 改回备份内容：`sudo cp /etc/fstab.backup.20261107174449 /etc/fstab`（即 `defaults,nofail 0 2`），否则重启又变只读。

message.content:
现在有一个新的科研任务。请你先不要直接下载完整数据集，也不要影响服务器当前正在运行的科研任务/GPU任务。这个任务目前主要是网络、磁盘和数据检查，原则上 CPU-only 即可。

背景：

我们现有的 video captioning 工作使用 MSR-VTT/MSVD，检索库主要来自 benchmark 自己的 training split。现在导师希望把检索库扩大成一个独立的大规模外部视频库，模拟更接近“联网检索”的效果。

目前首选候选数据集是：

VideoUFO
Hugging Face dataset:
VideoUFO/VideoUFO
或 WenhaoWang/VideoUFO（请你自行核对官方/镜像仓库以及文件结构）

公开资料显示：
- 约 1.09M video clips
- 总仓库约 911GB
- 视频本体约 800GB 左右
- 有 brief caption 和 detailed caption
- 视频文件应该已经实际托管在 Hugging Face，而不是像 Panda-2M 那样只提供 URL/metadata
- 数据以若干 tar/shard 文件形式保存
- 最终科研用途是把它作为 external retrieval corpus，而不是拿它替换 MSR-VTT/MSVD 测试集

服务器可用于这项任务的磁盘空间大约 4TB，但不要默认这个数字绝对准确，先实际检查。

你的任务分成以下几个阶段。

一、先检查服务器当前状态

请检查并汇报：

1. 当前所有磁盘/分区的总容量、已用容量、可用容量、挂载路径。
2. 找出最适合存放 VideoUFO 的磁盘/目录。
3. 确认目标盘至少有足够空间容纳：
   - 约 0.9TB 原始数据
   - 后续视频特征
   - embedding / FAISS index
   - 临时文件
   - 实验输出
4. 不要碰现有科研数据，不要删除任何文件。
5. 检查是否有正在运行的重要 GPU/CPU/网络任务，尤其不要中断现有实验。
6. 如果当前存在大规模下载、GPU生成或其他关键任务，只做只读检查和小文件测试。

二、核对 VideoUFO 的真实下载情况

请你不要相信网页上的容量描述，必须实际核对 Hugging Face 仓库。

确认：

1. dataset repo 是否真实存在。
2. 视频文件是不是实际托管在 Hugging Face，而不是只有 YouTube URL。
3. 仓库总大小。
4. 视频文件总大小。
5. shard/tar 文件数量。
6. 单个 shard 大约多大。
7. metadata/caption 文件有哪些。
8. metadata 中至少确认：
   - video/clip ID
   - brief caption
   - detailed caption
   - 视频文件与 metadata 的对应关系
9. license。
10. 是否需要 gated access/token。
11. 是否存在 Git LFS / Xet / hf_transfer 等特殊下载机制。

请把你实际看到的文件名、大小和目录结构记录下来。

三、只做“小规模真实下载测试”

绝对不要直接开始完整 900GB 下载。

先找一个尽可能有代表性的最小视频 shard，或者从一个 shard 中只下载可测试的数据。

至少测试以下下载方式：

A. Hugging Face 官方 endpoint
B. hf-mirror（如果服务器环境可用）
C. huggingface-cli / hf download
D. 如果仓库使用 Xet，测试当前机器的 Xet 下载情况
E. 如果可用，可以测试 aria2 / wget 等，但不要为了测速搞破坏性操作

每种可行方案记录：

- 实际平均速度
- 峰值速度
- 是否稳定
- 是否频繁断流
- 是否支持 resume
- CPU占用
- 磁盘写入速度
- 是否出现 timeout / 403 / 401 / xet error / LFS error
- 估算完整 911GB 下载需要多久

注意：

不要只测速几十秒就下结论。
尽量获得一个有代表性的持续测速结果，但也不要浪费大量流量。

四、验证下载下来的东西是不是真视频

从实际下载的数据中随机抽取至少几十个样本。

检查：

1. 是否能正常解包。
2. 是否真的是 mp4/webm/其他视频，而不是 URL 文件。
3. ffprobe 能否正常读取。
4. 随机记录：
   - 视频时长
   - 分辨率
   - fps
   - codec
   - 文件大小
5. 是否有损坏视频。
6. video ID 是否可以和 metadata 对上。
7. brief caption 是否存在。
8. detailed caption 是否存在。
9. 随机检查至少 20–50 个 video-caption pair，确认 caption 和视频内容大体匹配。

如果环境允许，可以抽帧检查，但不要因此占用大量 GPU。

五、特别检查它适不适合我们现有科研 pipeline

我们现在不是做 text-to-video，而是做 retrieval-augmented video captioning。

请检查这个数据集是否可以比较自然地用于：

query video
→ video/text embedding
→ FAISS/ANN retrieval
→ top-K external videos
→ reranking
→ retrieved video feature
→ cross-gating/fusion
→ caption generation

重点判断：

1. 每个 clip 是否有稳定唯一 ID。
2. 每个 clip 是否有独立 caption。
3. clip 粒度是否合适。
4. 是否存在大量来自同一个 source video 的重复切片。
5. 是否会导致 retrieval 结果高度重复。
6. 是否能方便建立 10K / 50K / 100K / 250K / 500K / full 1.09M 的嵌套子集。
7. brief caption 与 detailed caption 哪个更适合做 retrieval embedding。
8. 原视频和 caption 是否足够适合 X-CLIP / ViCLIP / Video-LLaMA 一类模型。
9. 是否存在明显的 domain 偏差，例如大量 animation、AI-generated、instructional-only、sports-only 等。
10. 是否明显比 MSR-VTT/MSVD 更开放域。

六、数据泄漏/重合风险

后面我们还要在 MSR-VTT/MSVD 上测试，所以现在就先检查可行性。

不要现在做昂贵的全库 duplicate detection，但请研究并汇报：

1. VideoUFO 的来源。
2. 是否可能与 MSR-VTT/MSVD 来源重叠。
3. metadata 是否保留 source URL / YouTube ID / source video ID。
4. 后续是否能通过：
   - URL/source ID
   - video hash
   - perceptual hash
   - embedding similarity
   来排除 test-set duplicate / near-duplicate。

如果官方论文或 dataset card 有 claimed overlap statistics，也记录下来，但要和你自己的实际检查区分开。

七、不要做的事情

目前禁止：

- 不要直接下载完整 900GB。
- 不要直接解压全部数据。
- 不要开始全库 feature extraction。
- 不要开始 FAISS 全量建库。
- 不要修改我们现有论文实验代码。
- 不要占用 A6000 跑无关任务。
- 不要删除已有数据。
- 不要为了腾空间清理任何旧实验。
- 不要因为某一个下载方案失败，就直接判定整个数据集不可用。

这一步的目的只是回答：

“VideoUFO 对我们这台服务器来说，究竟是不是一个真实可下载、可用、适合作为大规模外部 video retrieval corpus 的数据集？”

八、最后给我一个明确结论

最终报告请尽量通俗，至少包含：

1. VideoUFO 是否真实可下载：
   PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

2. 当前服务器下载是否现实：
   PASS / SLOW_BUT_USABLE / IMPRACTICAL / FAIL

3. 实际最佳下载方式。

4. 实测下载速度。

5. 预计完整下载约 911GB 需要多久。

6. 实际可用磁盘空间。

7. 下载完整数据后预计还剩多少空间。

8. 是否存在“压缩包+解压后文件同时存在导致空间爆掉”的风险。

9. 视频是否真实存在且可正常解码。

10. metadata 是否能和视频一一对应。

11. caption 是否适合 retrieval。

12. 是否适合我们的 external video RAG / video captioning 研究。

13. 和之前 Panda-2M 的核心区别：
    - Panda 是不是主要只有 URL/metadata
    - VideoUFO 是不是实际托管视频
    - 为什么这个在当前服务器上更现实

14. 你认为是否应该正式下载全量：
    YES / YES_WITH_CONDITIONS / NO

15. 如果 YES，给出正式下载方案，但先不要实际执行全量下载。

所有结论都尽量基于你在服务器上的真实测试，而不是只引用网页说明。

如果发现 VideoUFO 实际情况与公开资料不一致，以服务器真实检查结果为准。

最后请保留完整命令、日志位置、测速数据和检查结果，方便后续复核。

Here's a summary of the VideoUFO paper (arXiv:2503.01739), "VideoUFO: A Million-Scale User-Focused Dataset for Text-to-Video Generation" by Wenhao Wang & Yi Yang (UTS), submitted Mar 3, 2025; accepted at NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks Track.

**Core idea & sources:**
- First text-to-video dataset curated around **real users' focused topics**. Topics are identified by clustering the million-scale real T2V prompt dataset **VidProM**, yielding **1,291 user-focused topics**.
- For each topic, videos are retrieved **exclusively via YouTube's official API**, restricted to **Creative Commons–licensed** videos (≤500 min, ≥720p... the HTML garbles resolution, but a quality/resolution filter applies).
- Videos are segmented into semantically consistent short clips following the **Panda-70M** pipeline (shot boundary detection, stitching, splitting).

**Scale & annotation:**
- **~1.09 million video clips** total.
- Each clip is paired with **both a brief and a detailed caption**:
  - Brief captions from the Panda-70M video captioning model.
  - Detailed captions from an Open-Sora v1.3.0–style pipeline (Plan-QWen2-VL 7B annotation).
- Each data point includes: clip + ID, topic, start/end times in the original video, brief caption, detailed caption, and a human-aligned quality score.
- Clips are verified against topics via GPT-4o-mini on detailed captions.

**Overlap with existing datasets (incl. MSR-VTT):**
- Claims **minimal overlap of only 0.29%** with existing video datasets — i.e., it introduces novel content rather than duplicating sources like MSR-VTT, Panda-70M, etc.

**Experiments/findings:**
- 16 current T2V models don't perform consistently across user-focused topics.

Here's a summary of the VideoUFO paper (arXiv:2503.01739), "VideoUFO: A Million-Scale User-Focused Dataset for Text-to-Video Generation" by Wenhao Wang & Yi Yang (UTS), submitted Mar 3, 2025; accepted at NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks Track.

**Core idea & sources:**
- First text-to-video dataset curated around **real users' focused topics**. Topics are identified by clustering the million-scale real T2V prompt dataset **VidProM**, yielding **1,291 user-focused topics**.
- For each topic, videos are retrieved **exclusively via YouTube's official API**, restricted to **Creative Commons–licensed** videos (≤500 min, ≥720p... the HTML garbles resolution, but a quality/resolution filter applies).
- Videos are segmented into semantically consistent short clips following the **Panda-70M** pipeline (shot boundary detection, stitching, splitting).

**Scale & annotation:**
- **~1.09 million video clips** total.
- Each clip is paired with **both a brief and a detailed caption**:
  - Brief captions from the Panda-70M video captioning model.
  - Detailed captions from an Open-Sora v1.3.0–style pipeline (Plan-QWen2-VL 7B annotation).
- Each data point includes: clip + ID, topic, start/end times in the original video, brief caption, detailed caption, and a human-aligned quality score.
- Clips are verified against topics via GPT-4o-mini on detailed captions.

**Overlap with existing datasets (incl. MSR-VTT):**
- Claims **minimal overlap of only 0.29%** with existing video datasets — i.e., it introduces novel content rather than duplicating sources like MSR-VTT, Panda-70M, etc.

**Experiments/findings:**
- 16 current T2V models don't perform consistently across user-focused topics.
- A simple model trained on VideoUFO outperforms others on the **worst-performing topics**.

**Availability:** Hugging Face (`WenhaoWang/VideoUFO`) and GitHub (`WangWenhao0716/BenchUFO`), under **CC BY 4.0**; also scalable to ~10M clips.

Note: the search results confirm the paper's **0.29% overlap** claim but do not contain a specific per-dataset breakdown against MSR-VTT — if you need the exact MSR-VTT overlap figure, the comparison table in the paper's Section 2 / Appendix would be the place to check.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.
