Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

query.description: The search query to use

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Metadata analysis for VideoUFO probe (CPU only, read-only input).

Usage: python analyze_meta.py <parquet-or-csv> [more files...]
Writes summary JSON to stdout and to meta_summary.json.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import collections
import statistics

OUT = {}


def parquet_rows(path, limit=None):
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    cols = ['ID', 'Topic', 'Brief_Caption', 'Detailed_Caption',
            'Start_Time', 'End_Time']
    pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
    have = set(pf.schema_arrow.names)
    cols = [c for c in cols if c in have]
    n = 0
    for batch in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=20000, columns=cols):
        d = batch.to_pydict()
        m = len(d[cols[0]])
        for i in range(m):
            yield {c: d[c][i] for c in cols}
            n += 1
            if limit and n >= limit:
                return


def main(paths):
    ids = []
    srcs = collections.Counter()
    topics = collections.Counter()
    brief_len = []
    detail_len = []
    missing_brief = missing_detail = 0
    dup = collections.Counter()
    n = 0
    for p in paths:
        if p.endswith('.parquet'):
            it = parquet_rows(p)
        else:
            import csv
            f = open(p, newline='', encoding='utf-8')
            r = csv.DictReader(f)
            it = ({'ID': row['ID'], 'Topic': row['Topic'],
                   'Brief_Caption': row['Brief Caption'],
                   'Detailed_Caption': row['Detailed Caption'],
                   'Start_Time': row['Start Time'], 'End_Time': row['End Time']}
                  for row in r)
        for row in it:
            n += 1
            i = row['ID']
            ids.append(i)
            dup[i] += 1
            srcs[i.split('.')[0]] += 1
            topics[row.get('Topic')] += 1
            b = (row.get('Brief_Caption') or '').strip()
            d = (row.get('Detailed_Caption') or '').strip()
            if not b:
                missing_brief += 1
            else:
                brief_len.append(len(b.split()))
            if not d:
                missing_detail += 1
            else:
                detail_len.append(len(d.split()))

    per_src = collections.Counter(srcs.values())
    res = {
        'rows': n,
        'unique_clip_ids': len(dup),
        'duplicate_clip_ids': sum(1 for v in dup.values() if v > 1),
        'unique_source_ids': len(srcs),
        'clips_per_source': dict(sorted(per_src.items())[:20]),
        'max_clips_per_source': max(srcs.values()) if srcs else 0,
        'top_sources': srcs.most_common(10),
        'unique_topics': len(topics),
        'top_topics': topics.most_common(15),
        'missing_brief': missing_brief,
        'missing_detailed': missing_detail,
        'brief_words': {'min': min(brief_len), 'median': statistics.median(brief_len),
                        'p90': sorted(brief_len)[int(.9 * len(brief_len))],
                        'max': max(brief_len)},
        'detail_words': {'min': min(detail_len), 'median': statistics.median(detail_len),
                         'p90': sorted(detail_len)[int(.9 * len(detail_len))],
                         'max': max(detail_len)},
    }
    # exact source-ID overlap with MSRVTT/MSVD test sets
    ev = json.load(open('/home/bn/videoufo_probe/eval_ytids.json'))
    src_set = set(srcs)
    res['overlap_with_eval'] = {}
    for k, v in ev.items():
        s = set(v)
        inter = src_set & s
        res['overlap_with_eval'][k] = {
            'eval_sources': len(s),
            'overlap_sources': len(inter),
            'overlap_examples': sorted(inter)[:10],
            'eval_source_frac': round(len(inter) / len(s), 5) if s else None,
        }
    json.dump(res, open('/home/bn/videoufo_probe/meta_summary.json', 'w'), indent=1)
    print(json.dumps(res, indent=1)[:4000])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1:])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parallel, resumable HTTP range downloader for hf-mirror URLs.

Usage: pget.py URL OUTFILE [--conns N] [--retries R]
Writes OUTFILE.partNNN chunks next to OUTFILE, then concatenates.
Safe to re-run: completed chunks are skipped.
"""
import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time


def head_size(url):
    out = subprocess.run(['curl', '-sIL', '--max-time', '60', url],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    size = None
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if line.lower().startswith('content-length:'):
            size = int(line.split(':', 1)[1].strip())
    return size


def fetch(url, start, end, path, retries):
    expected = end - start + 1
    for attempt in range(1, retries + 1):
        have = os.path.getsize(path) if os.path.exists(path) else 0
        if have >= expected:
            return True
        s = start + have
        cmd = ['curl', '-sL', '--max-time', '900', '--retry', '3',
               '--retry-delay', '5', '-r', f'{s}-{end}', url, '--append', '-o', path]
        subprocess.run(cmd)
        if os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) >= expected:
            return True
        time.sleep(min(30, 3 * attempt))
    return os.path.getsize(path) >= expected if os.path.exists(path) else False


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('url')
    ap.add_argument('out')
    ap.add_argument('--conns', type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument('--retries', type=int, default=8)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    size = head_size(a.url)
    if not size:
        sys.exit('cannot determine size')
    print(f'size={size} conns={a.conns}', flush=True)
    step = (size + a.conns - 1) // a.conns
    procs = []
    for i in range(a.conns):
        start = i * step
        end = min(size - 1, start + step - 1)
        if start > end:
            break
        path = f'{a.out}.part{i:03d}'
        p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, __file__, '--worker', a.url,
                              str(start), str(end), path, str(a.retries)])
        procs.append((p, path, end - start + 1))
    ok = True
    for p, path, want in procs:
        p.wait()
        got = os.path.getsize(path) if os.path.exists(path) else 0
        if got < want:
            ok = False
            print(f'chunk incomplete {path} {got}/{want}', flush=True)
    if not ok:
        sys.exit(1)
    with open(a.out, 'wb') as fo:
        for _, path, _ in procs:
            with open(path, 'rb') as fi:
                while True:
                    b = fi.read(1 << 20)
                    if not b:
                        break
                    fo.write(b)
    got = os.path.getsize(a.out)
    print(f'done {a.out} {got}/{size}', flush=True)
    if got != size:
        sys.exit(2)
    for _, path, _ in procs:
        os.remove(path)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == '--worker':
        _, _, url, start, end, path, retries = sys.argv
        sys.exit(0 if fetch(url, int(start), int(end), path, int(retries)) else 1)
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Join extracted shard-200 clips with metadata captions and build contact sheets.

Reads VideoUFO.csv (or parquet), filters rows whose ID is among samples/VideoUFO/*.mp4,
decodes a middle frame for each selected clip and writes caption_sheet_<n>.jpg.
"""
import csv
import glob
import io
import os
import sys

import av
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

ROOT = '/home/bn/videoufo_probe'
CLIPS = os.path.join(ROOT, 'samples', 'VideoUFO')

def load_meta(path):
    out = {}
    if path.endswith('.parquet'):
        import pyarrow.parquet as pq
        pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
        for b in pf.iter_batches(batch_size=20000,
                                 columns=['ID', 'Topic', 'Brief_Caption', 'Detailed_Caption',
                                          'Start_Time', 'End_Time']):
            d = b.to_pydict()
            for i in range(len(d['ID'])):
                out[d['ID'][i]] = {k: d[k][i] for k in d}
    else:
        with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            for r in csv.DictReader(f):
                out[r['ID']] = r
    return out


def frame(path, frac=0.4):
    c = av.open(path)
    dur = float(c.duration / 1e6) if c.duration else 2.0
    target = dur * frac
    im = None
    for f in c.decode(video=0):
        im = f.to_image()
        t = float(f.pts * f.time_base) if f.pts is not None else 0
        if t >= target:
            break
    return im


def main(csv_path, want=12, cols=3):
    meta = load_meta(csv_path)
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CLIPS, '*.mp4')))
    picked = []
    for f in files:
        cid = os.path.basename(f)[:-4]
        if cid in meta:
            picked.append((cid, f, meta[cid]))
        if len(picked) >= want:
            break
    print('matched', len(picked), 'of', len(files), 'clips in', os.path.basename(csv_path),
          '| meta rows', len(meta))
    if not picked:
        return
    rows = (len(picked) + cols - 1) // cols
    sheet = Image.new('RGB', (cols * 400, rows * 350), 'white')
    dr = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
    for i, (cid, f, m) in enumerate(picked):
        im = frame(f).resize((390, 220))
        x = (i % cols) * 400 + 5
        y = (i // cols) * 350 + 5
        sheet.paste(im, (x, y))
        brief = (m.get('Brief_Caption') or m.get('Brief Caption') or '')[:95]
        dr.text((x, y + 224), cid, fill='black')
        dr.text((x, y + 238), brief, fill='black')
        print(f'{cid}\t{m.get("Topic")}\t{brief}')
    out = os.path.join(ROOT, 'caption_sheet.jpg')
    sheet.save(out, quality=85)
    print('saved', out)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 12)

# VideoUFO feasibility probe — raw measurements (2026-11-14)

All tests run on this host, CPU-only, while the user's Qwen3.5-27B-FP8 GPU job ran
(~43 GB VRAM, 100% util). No GPU work was performed.

## Host / disk

- `/dev/sda` ext4 7.2 TiB, 3.0 TiB used, **3.9 TiB free — mounted `ro,relatime,norecovery`**
  (fstab `ro,noload,nofail`, unchanged since 2026-11-07 17:44).
- `/dev/nvme0n1p2` ext4 3.6 TiB, 885 GiB used, **2.5 TiB free — writable** (root fs).
- Network: wlp0s20f3 (WiFi, -54 dBm, 1080 Mbit PHY), 192.168.31.127. `eno1` has no
  working uplink. No proxy configured.

## Connectivity

| host | result |
|---|---|
| huggingface.co | timeout (curl exit 7 / 000) |
| cdn-lfs.huggingface.co | timeout |
| hf-mirror.com | 200 |
| modelscope.cn | 302 (no VideoUFO dataset there) |
| github.com / arxiv.org | 200 |

## Repo verification (hf-mirror API, 2026-11-14)

- `VideoUFO/VideoUFO` and `WenhaoWang/VideoUFO` are the same content, 302 files,
  **848.6 GiB** (911 GB).
- `VideoUFO_tar/`: **200 tar shards, 804.77 GiB**; min 158.74 MiB (VideoUFO_200.tar),
  median 4.34 GiB, max 4.64 GiB.
- `data/`: 93 parquet (`Full-00000..92-of-00093`), 42.67 GiB, 1,091,712 rows.
- `VideoUFO.csv`: 1.15 GiB.
- Fields: ID, Topic, Detailed_Caption, Brief_Caption, Start_Time, End_Time,
  Aesthetic_Quality, Background_Consistency, Dynamic_Degree, Imaging_Quality,
  Motion_Smoothness, Subject_Consistency (+ Middle_Frame image in parquet).
- license: cc-by-4.0, gated: false.
- Storage: Git LFS pointers + **Xet** (resolve redirects to cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co).

## Download tests

| method | file | bytes | time | rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| curl direct huggingface.co | VideoUFO_200.tar | 0 | 8.2 s | FAIL (conn) |
| curl hf-mirror, 1 conn | VideoUFO_200.tar | 4.46 MB | 45 s | **0.10 MB/s** |
| curl hf-mirror, 6 conns | VideoUFO_200.tar | 52 MB | 30 s | 1.7 MB/s |
| curl hf-mirror, 16 conns | VideoUFO_200.tar | 24.5 MB | 20 s | 1.23 MB/s |
| `hf download` (hf_xet 1.7) | VideoUFO_200.tar | 166.45 MB | 79.8 s | **2.09 MB/s** |
| `hf download` (hf_xet) | Full-00000.parquet | 335/470 MB | stalled | ~2.9 MB/s until stall |
| `hf download` + `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1` | Full-00000.parquet | 470 MB | see below | burst ~10 MB/s, then ~1.2 MB/s |
| tuna mirror (control, 60 s) | ls-lR.gz | 39.7 MB | 60 s | **6.27 MB/s sustained** |

Notes:
- xet downloads **stall** mid-file (observed twice at ~335 MB of 470 MB; concurrency
  pinned at 64, NIC drops to ~0.1 MB/s, no error in the xet log).
- Killing and restarting produced a **new `.incomplete`** (different etag suffix) and
  restarted from 0 — no resume observed for the xet path.
- The GPU job was unaffected (100% util, 86 °C throughout).

## Shard 200 contents (158.74 MiB, fully downloaded and extracted)

- 197 files, all `.mp4`, flat under `VideoUFO/`.
- Names: `<youtube_id>.<clip_index>.mp4`, e.g. `GceTUn_OH_Q.9.mp4`.
- 197 unique clip IDs, 166 unique YouTube source IDs (1.19 clips/source in this shard).
- Decode test (PyAV 15.1, no GPU): **197/197 decode OK, 0 bad**.
- Codec: mpeg4 (MPEG-4 Part 2) in all 197; no h264.
- Resolution: 640x360 (93), 360x640 (68), 360x360 (8), 270x480 (9), misc small.
  Landscape 95 / portrait 94 / square 8.
- FPS: 30 (112), 25 (33), 29.97 (32), 24 (8), 23.98 (5), misc.
- Duration: min 2.0 s, median 5.27 s, p90 35.0 s, max 165.0 s; 44% ≤5 s.
- File size: median 0.43 MB, max 8.57 MB.
- Frame sanity: 40/40 first frames decoded, none blank (std 19-102).
- dHash near-duplicate scan on first frames: 9 pairs with hamming ≤4 (several at 0,
  likely flat/dark frames — needs visual confirmation before calling duplicates).

## Metadata (from 4 MB CSV prefix only so far)

- Columns as above; 3,704 rows in the first 4 MB (≈1.07 M rows estimated for 1.15 GB).
- ID format `{youtube_id}.{index}` (e.g. `---MaV1RQGE.0`), 11-char YouTube ID.
- Brief caption: median 13 words (min 6, max 300).
- Detailed caption: median 136 words (min 48, max 491).
- 727 distinct topics in the first 3,704 rows (paper claims 1,291 overall).
- No source URL column; the YouTube ID is recoverable from the ID prefix.

## Ground truth for leakage tests

- MSR-VTT test: 2,990 videos → **2,151 unique YouTube IDs** (`url` field).
- MSR-VTT train+val: 7,010 → 5,029 unique.
- MSVD test: 670 → **522 unique YouTube IDs** (filenames).
- Paper claims 0.29% overlap with existing video datasets (verified from arXiv HTML).

## 5. Metadata 全量统计（1,091,712 行）

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 行数 | **1,091,712**（与 dataset card 一致） |
| 唯一 clip ID | 1,091,712（无重复 ID） |
| 唯一 YouTube source | **345,437** |
| clips / source | 平均 3.16，最大 **72**（长尾明显） |
| Topic | **1,289**（论文称 1,291） |
| Brief caption | 中位 13 词，p90 20，max 300，无缺失 |
| Detailed caption | 中位 137 词，p90 227，max 507，无缺失 |

单 shard 的 clips/source 分布：45% source 只有 1 个 clip，其余 2–72 个。

## 6. 与 MSR-VTT / MSVD 的泄漏检查（实际执行）

从本地标注提取 YouTube ID：
- MSR-VTT test：2,990 视频 → **2,151** 唯一 YouTube ID
- MSR-VTT train+val：7,010 → **5,029**
- MSVD test：670 → **522**

与 VideoUFO 全量 345,437 个 source ID 求交：

| 对比集 | 交集 source 数 |
|---|---|
| MSR-VTT test | **0** |
| MSR-VTT train+val | **0** |
| MSVD test | **0** |

论文自称与已有视频数据集重叠 0.29%（arXiv 2503.01739）；我们的实测显示
**至少在 YouTube 源 ID 层面，与这三个评测集无重合**。注意：
- 这是精确 ID 匹配，捕获不到“同一素材被重新上传/剪辑”的情况；
- 后续仍建议对 test 集做 pHash / embedding 近邻检查（成本低，可离线做）。

现有 EVCap 检索链路：query video → X-CLIP 特征 → 相似度检索 → 取回视频
（[32,768] 特征 + caption）→ cross-gating fusion → 生成。VideoUFO 能较自然地嵌入：

- **唯一 ID 稳定**：`{ytid}.{idx}`，1,091,712 个，无重复 ✔
- **每个 clip 独立 caption**：brief + detailed，无缺失 ✔
- **粒度**：中位 5.3 s，接近 MSVD/MSR-VTT 片段，适合 8/16 帧采样 ✔
- **同源重复切片**：平均 3.16 clips/source，最多 72 → **top-K 检索必须做 source 级去重/MMR**，
  否则 7 条结果可能来自同一视频 ⚠
- **嵌套子集**：可按 ID 哈希或 topic 分层抽样，10K/50K/100K/250K/500K/full 均可构造 ✔
- **brief vs detailed**：brief（13 词）更接近 MSR-VTT 字幕风格，适合做检索 embedding；
  detailed（137 词）适合 rerank / 质量打分 ⚠ 建议两路都用
- **模型兼容**：mpeg4/360p 可被 decord/PyAV/X-CLIP 正常读取；竖屏占一半，
  与 MSR-VTT 全横屏分布不同，需注意预处理一致性
- **域偏差**：topic 源自 VidProM 用户 prompt（digital/ocean/filmmaking/food/…），
  偏“创作/素材/短视频”风格，含大量竖屏、字幕烧录、动画/游戏画面；
  比 MSR-VTT/MSVD 更开放，但不是纯自然场景分布 ⚠
- **特征成本**：
  - X-CLIP 检索 embedding（512–768 维）全量约 2–4 GB，GPU 约 10–20 小时
  - EVCap fusion 用的 [32,768] 视频特征约 49 KB/clip → 全量 **~53 GB**，
    若用 ViT-G 全量预计算需 **100+ GPU 小时**；建议只对检索到的 top-K 在线计算并缓存

## 8. 磁盘规划

| 项 | 大小 |
|---|---|
| 原始下载（tar+parquet+csv） | 848.6 GiB |
| 解压后的视频 | ~805 GiB |
| 若 tar 与解压文件同时保留 | **1.61 TiB**（有撑爆风险） |
| X-CLIP embedding + FAISS | ~10 GB |
| fusion 特征（可选全量） | ~53 GB |

- 推荐落盘 8 TB 盘：3.9 TiB 可用 → 全部保留后仍余 ~2.2 TiB；
- 若只能用系统盘（2.5 TiB）：按“**每 shard 下载→校验→解压→删 tar**”流水线，
  峰值只多 4.3 GB，最终 ~805 GiB + 特征，剩余 ~1.6 TiB，可行但不推荐长期存放；
- 空间爆掉风险：**存在**（同时保留 tar 和解压文件时 1.61 TiB），用上面的流水线可完全避免。

## 9. 最终判断

1. **VideoUFO 真实可下载**：PASS
2. **当前服务器下载现实性**：SLOW_BUT_USABLE（速度波动大，需断点/重试策略）
3. **最佳方式**：`HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1 hf download ...`
   （hf_xet 1.7.0；直连 HF 不可用，curl 单连接不可用）
4. **实测速度**：0.10–19.8 MB/s，典型 5–10 MB/s
5. **911 GB 预计**：约 **13–50 小时**（按 20 / 5 MB/s）
6. **实际可用磁盘**：8 TB 盘 3.9 TiB（只读）；系统盘 2.5 TiB（可写）
7. **全量下载后剩余**：8 TB 盘 ~2.2 TiB；系统盘 ~1.6 TiB（用流水线）
8. **空间爆掉风险**：有，靠“下载即解压即删”规避
9. **视频真实可解码**：是（197/197）
10. **metadata 与视频一一对应**：是（197/197 join 成功）
11. **caption 适合 retrieval**：是（brief 13 词中位；detailed 137 词）
12. **适合 external video RAG**：适合，需处理同源多切片、竖屏、域偏差
13. **与 Panda-2M 的核心区别**：
    - Panda-2M 只发 metadata/YouTube URL，视频需自行从 YouTube 抓取（本机不可达）；
    - VideoUFO **视频真实托管在 HF**（200 个 tar，804.8 GiB），可直接下载；
    - 因此在本机（无 YouTube、仅 hf-mirror）VideoUFO 是唯一现实可得的百万级视频库。
14. **是否正式全量下载**：**YES_WITH_CONDITIONS**
15. **条件**：
    a. 8 TB 盘需恢复可写（当前只读；需人工 root 操作），或接受系统盘存放；
    b. 先下 metadata（1.2 GB）+ 5 个 shard 做端到端验证（解压/join/抽帧/特征各 1 次）；
    c. 按 shard 流水线下载，校验大小与 tar 完整性，失败重试；
    d. 下载期间不启动 GPU 特征提取（当前 GPU 任务优先）；
    e. 检索侧做 source 级去重，避免 top-K 同源。

```bash
python -c "import av; c=av.open('x.mp4'); print(c.streams.video[0].codec_context.name)"
```

- `/home/bn/videoufo_probe/NOTES.md`：原始测速与检查记录
- `dl_hfcli/VideoUFO_tar/VideoUFO_200.tar`：158.7 MB 完整 shard

现有 EVCap 检索链路：query video → X-CLIP 特征 → 相似度检索 → 取回视频

- **唯一 ID 稳定**：`{ytid}.{idx}`，1,091,712 个，无重复 ✔
- **每个 clip 独立 caption**：brief + detailed，无缺失 ✔

## 7. 是否适合现有 pipeline

（[32,768] 特征 + caption）→ cross-gating fusion → 生成。VideoUFO 能较自然地嵌入：

- **唯一 ID 稳定**：`{ytid}.{idx}`，1,091,712 个，无重复 ✔
- **每个 clip 独立 caption**：brief + detailed，无缺失 ✔
- **粒度**：中位 5.3 s，接近 MSVD/MSR-VTT 片段，适合 8/16 帧采样 ✔
- **同源重复切片**：平均 3.16 clips/source，最多 72 → **top-K 检索必须做 source 级去重/MMR**，
  否则 7 条结果可能来自同一视频 ⚠
- **嵌套子集**：可按 ID 哈希或 topic 分层抽样，10K/50K/100K/250K/500K/full 均可构造 ✔
- **brief vs detailed**：brief（13 词）更接近 MSR-VTT 字幕风格，适合做检索 embedding；
  detailed（137 词）适合 rerank / 质量打分 ⚠ 建议两路都用
- **模型兼容**：mpeg4/360p 可被 decord/PyAV/X-CLIP 正常读取；竖屏占一半，
  与 MSR-VTT 全横屏分布不同，需注意预处理一致性
- **域偏差**：topic 源自 VidProM 用户 prompt（digital/ocean/filmmaking/food/…），
  偏“创作/素材/短视频”风格，含大量竖屏、字幕烧录、动画/游戏画面；
  比 MSR-VTT/MSVD 更开放，但不是纯自然场景分布 ⚠
- **特征成本**：
  - X-CLIP 检索 embedding（512–768 维）全量约 2–4 GB，GPU 约 10–20 小时
  - EVCap fusion 用的 [32,768] 视频特征约 49 KB/clip → 全量 **~53 GB**，
    若用 ViT-G 全量预计算需 **100+ GPU 小时**；建议只对检索到的 top-K 在线计算并缓存

- codec：**mpeg4 (MPEG-4 Part 2)**，非 h264；分辨率以 360p 为主
  （640×360: 93，360×640: 68，其余更小）
- 时长：中位 5.27 s，p90 35 s，max 165 s；44% ≤5 s
- 文件大小：中位 0.43 MB
- 画幅：横向 95 / 纵向 94 / 方形 8（约一半是竖屏/Shorts 风格）
- 首帧非空白（40 帧亮度 std 19–102），但存在个别纯黑/纯白首帧（转场），
  抽帧做特征时应避开第 0 帧

**字幕对应验证**：
- 用全量 CSV join，197/197 全部命中，0 缺失
- 抽 12 对 caption-画面人工核对：**12/12 相符**（11 对完全一致，1 对画面偏暗但描述合理）

## 6. 与 MSR-VTT / MSVD 的泄漏检查（实际执行）

从本地标注提取 YouTube ID：
- MSR-VTT test：2,990 视频 → **2,151** 唯一 YouTube ID
- MSR-VTT train+val：7,010 → **5,029**
- MSVD test：670 → **522**

与 VideoUFO 全量 345,437 个 source ID 求交：

| 对比集 | 交集 source 数 |
|---|---|

论文自称与已有视频数据集重叠 0.29%（arXiv 2503.01739）；我们的实测显示
**至少在 YouTube 源 ID 层面，与这三个评测集无重合**。注意：
- 这是精确 ID 匹配，捕获不到“同一素材被重新上传/剪辑”的情况；
- 后续仍建议对 test 集做 pHash / embedding 近邻检查（成本低，可离线做）。

## 7. 是否适合现有 pipeline

现有 EVCap 检索链路：query video → X-CLIP 特征 → 相似度检索 → 取回视频
（[32,768] 特征 + caption）→ cross-gating fusion → 生成。VideoUFO 能较自然地嵌入：

- **唯一 ID 稳定**：`{ytid}.{idx}`，1,091,712 个，无重复 ✔
- **每个 clip 独立 caption**：brief + detailed，无缺失 ✔
- **粒度**：中位 5.3 s，接近 MSVD/MSR-VTT 片段，适合 8/16 帧采样 ✔
- **同源重复切片**：平均 3.16 clips/source，最多 72 → **top-K 检索必须做 source 级去重/MMR**，
  否则 7 条结果可能来自同一视频 ⚠
- **嵌套子集**：可按 ID 哈希或 topic 分层抽样，10K/50K/100K/250K/500K/full 均可构造 ✔
- **brief vs detailed**：brief（13 词）更接近 MSR-VTT 字幕风格，适合做检索 embedding；
  detailed（137 词）适合 rerank / 质量打分 ⚠ 建议两路都用
- **模型兼容**：mpeg4/360p 可被 decord/PyAV/X-CLIP 正常读取；竖屏占一半，
  与 MSR-VTT 全横屏分布不同，需注意预处理一致性
- **域偏差**：topic 源自 VidProM 用户 prompt（digital/ocean/filmmaking/food/…），
  偏“创作/素材/短视频”风格，含大量竖屏、字幕烧录、动画/游戏画面；
  比 MSR-VTT/MSVD 更开放，但不是纯自然场景分布 ⚠
- **特征成本**：
  - X-CLIP 检索 embedding（512–768 维）全量约 2–4 GB，GPU 约 10–20 小时
  - EVCap fusion 用的 [32,768] 视频特征约 49 KB/clip → 全量 **~53 GB**，
    若用 ViT-G 全量预计算需 **100+ GPU 小时**；建议只对检索到的 top-K 在线计算并缓存

**字幕对应验证**：
- 用全量 CSV join，197/197 全部命中，0 缺失

## 6. 与 MSR-VTT / MSVD 的泄漏检查（实际执行）

从本地标注提取 YouTube ID：
- MSR-VTT test：2,990 视频 → **2,151** 唯一 YouTube ID

## 7. 是否适合现有 pipeline

现有 EVCap 检索链路：query video → X-CLIP 特征 → 相似度检索 → 取回视频
（[32,768] 特征 + caption）→ cross-gating fusion → 生成。VideoUFO 能较自然地嵌入：

- **唯一 ID 稳定**：`{ytid}.{idx}`，1,091,712 个，无重复 ✔
- **每个 clip 独立 caption**：brief + detailed，无缺失 ✔
- **粒度**：中位 5.3 s，接近 MSVD/MSR-VTT 片段，适合 8/16 帧采样 ✔
- **同源重复切片**：平均 3.16 clips/source，最多 72 → **top-K 检索必须做 source 级去重/MMR**，
  否则 7 条结果可能来自同一视频 ⚠
- **嵌套子集**：可按 ID 哈希或 topic 分层抽样，10K/50K/100K/250K/500K/full 均可构造 ✔
- **brief vs detailed**：brief（13 词）更接近 MSR-VTT 字幕风格，适合做检索 embedding；

- **模型兼容**：mpeg4/360p 可被 decord/PyAV/X-CLIP 正常读取；竖屏占一半，
  与 MSR-VTT 全横屏分布不同，需注意预处理一致性
- **域偏差**：topic 源自 VidProM 用户 prompt（digital/ocean/filmmaking/food/…），
  偏“创作/素材/短视频”风格，含大量竖屏、字幕烧录、动画/游戏画面；
  比 MSR-VTT/MSVD 更开放，但不是纯自然场景分布 ⚠
- **特征成本**：
  - X-CLIP 检索 embedding（512–768 维）全量约 2–4 GB，A6000 约 5–10 GPU 小时
    （解码是 CPU 瓶颈：本机 32 核约 500 clips/s，1.09M 约 40 分钟）
  - EVCap fusion 用的 [32,768] 视频特征约 49 KB/clip → 全量 **~53 GB**，
    若用 ViT-G 全量预计算需 **100+ GPU 小时**；建议只对检索到的 top-K 在线计算并缓存

## 8. 磁盘规划

| 项 | 大小 |
|---|---|
| 原始下载（tar+parquet+csv） | 848.6 GiB |
| 解压后的视频 | ~805 GiB |
| 若 tar 与解压文件同时保留 | **1.61 TiB**（有撑爆风险） |
| X-CLIP embedding + FAISS | ~10 GB |
| fusion 特征（可选全量） | ~53 GB |

- 推荐落盘 8 TB 盘：3.9 TiB 可用 → 全部保留后仍余 ~2.2 TiB；
- 若只能用系统盘（2.5 TiB）：按“**每 shard 下载→校验→解压→删 tar**”流水线，
  峰值只多 4.3 GB，最终 ~805 GiB + 特征，剩余 ~1.6 TiB，可行但不推荐长期存放；
- 空间爆掉风险：**存在**（同时保留 tar 和解压文件时 1.61 TiB），用上面的流水线可完全避免。

## 9. 最终判断

1. **VideoUFO 真实可下载**：PASS
2. **当前服务器下载现实性**：SLOW_BUT_USABLE（速度波动大，需断点/重试策略）
3. **最佳方式**：`HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1 hf download ...`
   （hf_xet 1.7.0；直连 HF 不可用，curl 单连接不可用）
4. **实测速度**：0.10–19.8 MB/s，典型 5–10 MB/s
5. **911 GB 预计**：约 **13–50 小时**（按 20 / 5 MB/s）
6. **实际可用磁盘**：8 TB 盘 3.9 TiB（只读）；系统盘 2.5 TiB（可写）
7. **全量下载后剩余**：8 TB 盘 ~2.2 TiB；系统盘 ~1.6 TiB（用流水线）
8. **空间爆掉风险**：有，靠“下载即解压即删”规避
9. **视频真实可解码**：是（197/197）
10. **metadata 与视频一一对应**：是（197/197 join 成功）
11. **caption 适合 retrieval**：是（brief 13 词中位；detailed 137 词）
12. **适合 external video RAG**：适合，需处理同源多切片、竖屏、域偏差
13. **与 Panda-2M 的核心区别**：
    - Panda-2M 只发 metadata/YouTube URL，视频需自行从 YouTube 抓取（本机不可达）；
    - VideoUFO **视频真实托管在 HF**（200 个 tar，804.8 GiB），可直接下载；
    - 因此在本机（无 YouTube、仅 hf-mirror）VideoUFO 是唯一现实可得的百万级视频库。
14. **是否正式全量下载**：**YES_WITH_CONDITIONS**
15. **条件**：
    a. 8 TB 盘需恢复可写（当前只读；需人工 root 操作），或接受系统盘存放；

# VideoUFO feasibility probe — raw measurements (2026-11-14)

All tests run on this host, CPU-only, while the user's Qwen3.5-27B-FP8 GPU job ran
(~43 GB VRAM, 100% util). No GPU work was performed.

## Host / disk

- `/dev/sda` ext4 7.2 TiB, 3.0 TiB used, **3.9 TiB free — mounted `ro,relatime,norecovery`**
  (fstab `ro,noload,nofail`, unchanged since 2026-11-07 17:44).
- `/dev/nvme0n1p2` ext4 3.6 TiB, 885 GiB used, **2.5 TiB free — writable** (root fs).
- Network: wlp0s20f3 (WiFi, -54 dBm, 1080 Mbit PHY), 192.168.31.127. `eno1` has no
  working uplink. No proxy configured.

## Connectivity

| host | result |
|---|---|
| huggingface.co | timeout (curl exit 7 / 000) |
| cdn-lfs.huggingface.co | timeout |
| hf-mirror.com | 200 |
| modelscope.cn | 302 (no VideoUFO dataset there) |
| github.com / arxiv.org | 200 |

## Repo verification (hf-mirror API, 2026-11-14)

- `VideoUFO/VideoUFO` and `WenhaoWang/VideoUFO` are the same content, 302 files,
  **848.6 GiB** (911 GB).
- `VideoUFO_tar/`: **200 tar shards, 804.77 GiB**; min 158.74 MiB (VideoUFO_200.tar),
  median 4.34 GiB, max 4.64 GiB.
- `data/`: 93 parquet (`Full-00000..92-of-00093`), 42.67 GiB, 1,091,712 rows.
- `VideoUFO.csv`: 1.15 GiB.
- Fields: ID, Topic, Detailed_Caption, Brief_Caption, Start_Time, End_Time,
  Aesthetic_Quality, Background_Consistency, Dynamic_Degree, Imaging_Quality,
  Motion_Smoothness, Subject_Consistency (+ Middle_Frame image in parquet).
- license: cc-by-4.0, gated: false.
- Storage: Git LFS pointers + **Xet** (resolve redirects to cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co).

## Download tests

| method | file | bytes | time | rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| curl direct huggingface.co | VideoUFO_200.tar | 0 | 8.2 s | FAIL (conn) |
| curl hf-mirror, 1 conn | VideoUFO_200.tar | 4.46 MB | 45 s | **0.10 MB/s** |
| curl hf-mirror, 6 conns | VideoUFO_200.tar | 52 MB | 30 s | 1.7 MB/s |

| `hf download` (hf_xet) | Full-00000.parquet | 335/470 MB | stalled | ~2.9 MB/s until stall |
| `hf download` + `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1` | Full-00000.parquet | 473 MiB | **95 s** (01:31:32→01:33:07) | **5.2 MB/s avg**, peak ~12 MB/s, dip ~1.2 MB/s |
| `hf download` + `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1` | VideoUFO.csv 1,234,455,730 B | **62.25 s** | **19.8 MB/s avg** (retry after one throttled attempt) |
| tuna mirror (control, 60 s) | ls-lR.gz | 39.7 MB | 60 s | **6.27 MB/s sustained** |
| `hf download` + HIGH_PERF | VideoUFO_1.tar 3.9 GB | 1.73 GB at 88 s | ~20 MB/s sustained | NIC peaks 26–35 MB/s |

Notes:
- xet downloads **stall** mid-file (observed twice at ~335 MB of 470 MB; concurrency
  pinned at 64, NIC drops to ~0.1 MB/s, no error in the xet log).
- Killing and restarting produced a **new `.incomplete`** (different etag suffix) and
  restarted from 0 — no resume observed for the xet path.
- The GPU job was unaffected (100% util, 86 °C throughout).

## Shard 200 contents (158.74 MiB, fully downloaded and extracted)

- 197 files, all `.mp4`, flat under `VideoUFO/`.
- Names: `<youtube_id>.<clip_index>.mp4`, e.g. `GceTUn_OH_Q.9.mp4`.
- 197 unique clip IDs, 166 unique YouTube source IDs (1.19 clips/source in this shard).
- Decode test (PyAV 15.1, no GPU): **197/197 decode OK, 0 bad**.
- Codec: mpeg4 (MPEG-4 Part 2) in all 197; no h264.
- Resolution: 640x360 (93), 360x640 (68), 360x360 (8), 270x480 (9), misc small.
  Landscape 95 / portrait 94 / square 8.
- FPS: 30 (112), 25 (33), 29.97 (32), 24 (8), 23.98 (5), misc.
- Duration: min 2.0 s, median 5.27 s, p90 35.0 s, max 165.0 s; 44% ≤5 s.
- File size: median 0.43 MB, max 8.57 MB.
- Frame sanity: 40/40 first frames decoded, none blank (std 19-102).
- dHash near-duplicate scan on first frames: 9 pairs with hamming ≤4 (several at 0,
  likely flat/dark frames — needs visual confirmation before calling duplicates).

## Metadata (from 4 MB CSV prefix only so far)

- Columns as above; 3,704 rows in the first 4 MB (≈1.07 M rows estimated for 1.15 GB).
- ID format `{youtube_id}.{index}` (e.g. `---MaV1RQGE.0`), 11-char YouTube ID.
- Brief caption: median 13 words (min 6, max 300).
- Detailed caption: median 136 words (min 48, max 491).
- 727 distinct topics in the first 3,704 rows (paper claims 1,291 overall).
- No source URL column; the YouTube ID is recoverable from the ID prefix.

- MSR-VTT test: 2,990 videos → **2,151 unique YouTube IDs** (`url` field).
- MSR-VTT train+val: 7,010 → 5,029 unique.
- MSVD test: 670 → **522 unique YouTube IDs** (filenames).
- Paper claims 0.29% overlap with existing video datasets (verified from arXiv HTML).

content.text:
## 一、一句话结论

**VideoUFO 是真的：视频本体确实托管在 Hugging Face 上（200 个 tar、804.8 GiB），不是 Panda-2M 那种只有 URL 的元数据。本机用 `hf + Xet 高性能模式` 实测 **19.8–26.3 MB/s**，4.09 GB 的 shard 155.6 秒下完，按此推算完整 911 GB 约 **10–13 小时**。** 适合做外部检索库，但有一个现实前提：8 TB 数据盘现在仍是只读，真正能写的只有系统盘 2.5 TiB。

---

## 二、我实际做了什么（没有做的事也说明）

- ✅ 只读检查了磁盘、GPU/CPU 任务、网络
- ✅ 实际拉取了仓库文件树、下载了 3 个真实文件（158 MB shard、473 MiB parquet、1.23 GB CSV、4.09 GB shard）
- ✅ 解包并解码了 197 个 mp4，抽帧比对字幕
- ✅ 用全量 CSV 做了统计和泄漏检查
- ❌ 没有下载完整 911 GB；❌ 没有全量解压；❌ 没有跑特征提取/FAISS；❌ 没改现有论文代码；❌ 没占 GPU

全程你的 Qwen3.5-27B-FP8 任务保持 100% 利用率、86 °C 正常跑，未被干扰。

---

## 三、服务器现状

| 磁盘 | 容量 | 可用 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/dev/sda` 8 TB | 7.2 TiB | **3.9 TiB** | **只读**（`ro,norecovery`，11-07 起） |
| `/dev/nvme0n1p2` 系统盘 | 3.6 TiB | **2.5 TiB** | 可写 |

- 所谓“约 4 TB”就是那块 8 TB 盘，**但当前不可写**，需要人工 root 处理才能用于正式下载。
- 探测数据共 6.9 GB，全放在系统盘 `/home/bn/videoufo_probe/`，没有动 8 TB 盘，也没删任何已有数据。

---

## 四、仓库核对（实际 API 返回，不是网页描述）

`VideoUFO/VideoUFO` 与 `WenhaoWang/VideoUFO` 是同一份内容：

| 项 | 实测 |
|---|---|
| 文件总数 | 302 |
| 总大小 | **848.6 GiB ≈ 911 GB** |
| 视频 tar | **200 个，804.77 GiB**（最小 158.7 MiB，中位 4.34 GiB，最大 4.64 GiB） |
| metadata parquet | 93 个，42.67 GiB，**1,091,712 行** |
| metadata CSV | 1.15 GiB |
| license | **CC BY 4.0** |
| gated / token | **不需要** |
| 存储机制 | Git LFS + **Xet**（下载会 302 到 xethub） |

字段：`ID, Topic, Detailed_Caption, Brief_Caption, Start_Time, End_Time` + 6 个 VBench 质量分。

---

## 五、下载实测（同一台机器、同一 Wi-Fi）

| 方法 | 文件 | 大小 | 耗时 | 平均速度 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 直连 huggingface.co | — | — | 超时 | **失败** |
| curl + hf-mirror 单连接 | 158 MB shard | 4.5 MB | 45 s | 0.10 MB/s |
| curl 16 连接 | 158 MB shard | 24.5 MB | 20 s | 1.23 MB/s |
| `hf download` 默认 | 158 MB shard | 166 MB | 79.8 s | 2.09 MB/s |
| `hf download` 默认 | 473 MiB parquet | 335/470 MB | **卡死** | 中断后从 0 重下，无续传 |
| **`hf download` + `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1`** | 473 MiB parquet | 473 MiB | 95 s | **5.2 MB/s** |
| **同上** | CSV 1.23 GB | 1.23 GB | 62.3 s | **19.8 MB/s** |
| **同上** | **4.09 GB shard** | 4.09 GB | **155.6 s** | **26.3 MB/s** |

结论：
- **默认模式会中途卡死**（观察到 2 次），且重试不会续传；
- **高性能模式稳定且越下越快**，大文件反而跑满（并发自动升到 100+ 连接）；
- 所以正式下载必须用高性能模式 + 按 shard 重试，而不是单线程 curl。

**911 GB 预计：10–13 小时**（按 26.3 / 19.8 MB/s），保守 10 MB/s 约 25 小时。

---

## 六、视频真的存在且能解码吗？

从最小的 shard（`VideoUFO_200.tar`，158 MB）完整解出 **197 个 mp4**：

- **197/197 全部可解码**，0 损坏（PyAV，CPU）
- 编码：mpeg4（MPEG-4 Part 2，非 h264）；分辨率以 **360p** 为主（640×360、360×640）
- 时长：中位 **5.27 s**，p90 35 s，最长 165 s；44% ≤5 s
- 画幅：横向 95 / 竖屏 94 / 方形 8（约一半是竖屏）
- 首帧：40 个抽样全部非空白；少数转场帧接近纯黑/纯白

**字幕对应**：用全量 CSV join，**197/197 全部匹配**；抽 12 对做人工看图核对，**12/12 相符**。例如：

- `1eV3S6u7m3w.2` ↔ “A woman is standing in a kitchen, holding a glass of milk and drinking it” —— 画面正是女子在厨房喝奶
- `1ejao1E_Rk0.0` ↔ “A poster for mortal kombat x…” —— 画面正是 Mortal Kombat 海报
- `1eylP__4xSE.0` ↔ “greek inspired watermelon feta salad cups” —— 画面正是该文字海报

---

## 七、Metadata 全量统计（1,091,712 行）

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 唯一 clip ID | 1,091,712（无重复） |
| 唯一 YouTube 源视频 | **345,437** |
| 每个源的切片数 | 平均 **3.16**，最多 **72**；45% 的源只有 1 个切片 |
| Topic 数 | **1,289**（论文称 1,291） |
| Brief caption | 中位 **13 词**，p90 20，无缺失 |
| Detailed caption | 中位 **137 词**，p90 227，无缺失 |
| Brief caption 重复率 | **32.8% 的行其 brief 在库中重复**（最高频是一句 “a black background with white text on it.” 出现 1,723 次） |

Topic 分布较均衡：前 10 个 topic 只占约 2.6%。

---

## 八、数据泄漏检查（实际执行）

从本地标注提取 YouTube ID：MSR-VTT test 2,151 个源、MSR-VTT train+val 5,029 个、MSVD test 522 个。

|---|---|
| MSR-VTT test | **0** |
| MSR-VTT train+val | **0** |
| MSVD test | **0** |

# VideoUFO per-shard download -> verify -> extract -> delete pipeline.
# Resumable: completed shards are skipped; failed shards are retried in later passes.
set -u

BASE=/home/bn/datasets/VideoUFO
HF=/home/bn/videoufo_probe/hfenv/bin/hf
PY=/media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1/xyl/Display/repro_evcap/venv/bin/python

export HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1
export HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT=180
export HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1

LOG=$BASE/logs/download.log
STATE=$BASE/state
DONE=$STATE/completed_shards.txt
SIZES=$STATE/shard_sizes.tsv
TMP=$BASE/tmp
VID=$BASE/videos
mkdir -p "$BASE"/{videos,tmp,logs,metadata,state/shards} "$VID/VideoUFO"
touch "$DONE"

exec 9>"$STATE/lock"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "another supervisor instance holds the lock" >&2
  exit 3
fi

log() { printf '%s | %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >> "$LOG"; }
avail_gib() { df -BG --output=avail /home/bn | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
is_done() { grep -qx "$1" "$DONE" 2>/dev/null; }

log "supervisor start pid=$$ host=$(hostname) avail=$(avail_gib)GiB"

while :; do
  pass_ok=0
  pending=0
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do
    is_done "$i" && continue
    pending=$((pending+1))

    a=$(avail_gib)
    if [ "$a" -lt 500 ]; then
      log "shard $i | PAUSED | avail=${a}GiB below 500GiB gate; sleeping 1800s"
      sleep 1800
      continue
    elif [ "$a" -lt 800 ]; then
      log "shard $i | WARN | avail=${a}GiB below 800GiB"
    fi

    src="VideoUFO_tar/VideoUFO_$i.tar"
    exp=$(awk -v k="$i" '$1==k{print $2}' "$SIZES")
    if [ -z "${exp:-}" ]; then
      log "shard $i | FAIL | no expected size in $SIZES"
      continue
    fi

    ok=0
    for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
      rm -rf "$TMP/shard_$i"
      mkdir -p "$TMP/shard_$i"
      t0=$(date +%s)
      timeout 5400 "$HF" download VideoUFO/VideoUFO "$src" --repo-type dataset \

      if [ "$sz" = "$exp" ] && tar -tf "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        mbps=$(( sz / dt / 1048576 ))
        log "shard $i | DOWNLOADED | attempt=$attempt bytes=$sz secs=$dt mbps=$mbps avail=$(avail_gib)GiB"
        ok=1
        break
      fi
      log "shard $i | RETRY | attempt=$attempt rc=$rc bytes=$sz expected=$exp secs=$dt"
      sleep $(( 30 * attempt ))
    done

    if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
      log "shard $i | FAILED_ALL_ATTEMPTS | will retry in next pass"
      rm -rf "$TMP/shard_$i"
      continue
    fi

    # extract into scratch, verify, then move into place
    ex="$TMP/extract_$i"
    rm -rf "$ex"; mkdir -p "$ex"
    t0=$(date +%s)
    nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 tar -xf "$f" -C "$ex"
    xrc=$?
    want=$(tar -tf "$f" | grep -c '\.mp4$')
    have=$(find "$ex" -name '*.mp4' | wc -l)

      log "shard $i | EXTRACT_FAIL | rc=$xrc have=$have want=$want secs=$xt"
      rm -rf "$ex"
      continue
    fi

    dec=$(PYTHONPATH="$PYAV" "$PY" - "$ex" <<'PYEOF'
import sys, glob, random, av
files = glob.glob(sys.argv[1] + '/**/*.mp4', recursive=True)
random.seed(42)
sample = random.sample(files, min(5, len(files)))
bad = 0
for f in sample:
    try:

        for _ in c.decode(video=0):

    except Exception:

print(bad)
PYEOF

      rm -rf "$ex"

    moved=$(find "$ex" -name '*.mp4' | wc -l)

    rm -rf "$ex"

      "$i" "$sz" "$dt" "$want" "${dec:-0}" "$moved" "$(date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')" "$a" \
      > "$STATE/shards/VideoUFO_$i.json"
    log "shard $i | DONE | clips=$want moved=$moved total_videos=$total tar_deleted=yes avail=${a}GiB"

  done

for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
      rm -rf "$TMP/shard_$i"
      mkdir -p "$TMP/shard_$i"
      t0=$(date +%s)
      timeout 5400 "$HF" download VideoUFO/VideoUFO "$src" --repo-type dataset \
        --local-dir "$TMP/shard_$i" >> "$BASE/logs/shard_$i.log" 2>&1
      rc=$?
      f="$TMP/shard_$i/$src"
      sz=$(stat -c %s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
      t1=$(date +%s); dt=$(( t1 > t0 ? t1 - t0 : 1 ))
      if [ "$sz" = "$exp" ] && tar -tf "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        mbps=$(( sz / dt / 1048576 ))
        log "shard $i | DOWNLOADED | attempt=$attempt bytes=$sz secs=$dt mbps=$mbps avail=$(avail_gib)GiB"
        ok=1
        break
      fi
      log "shard $i | RETRY | attempt=$attempt rc=$rc bytes=$sz expected=$exp secs=$dt"
      sleep $(( 30 * attempt ))
    done

    if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
      log "shard $i | FAILED_ALL_ATTEMPTS | will retry in next pass"
      rm -rf "$TMP/shard_$i"
      continue
    fi

    # extract into scratch, verify, then move into place
    ex="$TMP/extract_$i"
    rm -rf "$ex"; mkdir -p "$ex"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Network watchdog: detect a dead/stalled uplink and force NetworkManager to
3	# re-associate instead of waiting for the driver to notice.
4	#
5	# Why: on 2026-11-11 19:06-19:24 the machine sat on iKuai5G-68ab while its
6	# uplink was dead; the portal-only wired port (eno1) became the IPv4 default
7	# route and the reverse SSH tunnel timed out for ~18 minutes.
8	#
9	# Recovery target is FIXED to one known-good access point:
10	#     connection Xiaomi_311 / interface wlp0s20f3 / gateway 192.168.31.1
11	#
12	# Health is judged from *that wireless connection's own gateway* - never from
13	# the system default route, which can legitimately be the campus portal on
14	# eno1 (172.20.64.1) and must not be treated as a Wi-Fi health signal.
15	#
16	# A healthy link is never touched.  Every action is rate limited to once per
17	# 60 s and logged to /home/bn/net_watchdog/watchdog.log.
18	#
19	#   ./net_watchdog.sh --check    # one probe, print state, do nothing
20	#   ./net_watchdog.sh            # run forever (systemd user service)
21	#   DRY_RUN=1 ./net_watchdog.sh  # log intended actions, execute nothing
22	#
23	# Test-only hooks (never set in production): SIM_ACTIVE_CON, SIM_CUR_GW.
24	set -u
25	
26	# --- fixed recovery target ------------------------------------------------
27	CON=${CON:-Xiaomi_311}              # preferred NetworkManager connection
28	DEV=${DEV:-wlp0s20f3}               # wireless interface
29	PREF_GW=${PREF_GW:-192.168.31.1}    # fallback only if the connection exposes no gateway
30	
31	# --- probing --------------------------------------------------------------
32	PROBE=${PROBE:-223.5.5.5}
33	INTERVAL=${INTERVAL:-15}
34	LOG=${LOG:-/home/bn/net_watchdog/watchdog.log}
35	MAXLOG=$((5 * 1024 * 1024))
36	DRY_RUN=${DRY_RUN:-0}
37	SIM_ACTIVE_CON=${SIM_ACTIVE_CON:-}
38	SIM_CUR_GW=${SIM_CUR_GW:-}
39	
40	GW_FAIL=0
41	NET_FAIL=0
42	LAST_ACT=-999
43	LAST_CUR=
44	STATE=OK
45	
46	ts() { date '+%F %T'; }
47	log() { echo "$(ts) $*" >>"$LOG"; }
48	
49	rotate() {
50	    [ -f "$LOG" ] || return 0
51	    [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG")" -gt "$MAXLOG" ] && mv -f "$LOG" "$LOG.1"
52	}
53	
54	probe() { ping -c1 -W2 -I "$DEV" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
55	
56	# Name of the NetworkManager connection currently active on $DEV (may be empty)
57	active_con() {
58	    if [ -n "$SIM_ACTIVE_CON" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$SIM_ACTIVE_CON"; return 0; fi
59	    nmcli -t -f NAME,DEVICE connection show --active 2>/dev/null |
60	        awk -F: -v d="$DEV" '$2==d{print $1; exit}'
61	}
62	
63	# IPv4 gateway configured for a connection - read dynamically, not from the
64	# global default route.
65	con_gw() {
66	    local g
67	    if [ -n "$SIM_CUR_GW" ] && [ "$1" = "$SIM_ACTIVE_CON" ]; then
68	        printf '%s\n' "$SIM_CUR_GW"; return 0
69	    fi
70	    g=$(nmcli -g IP4.GATEWAY connection show "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d ' ')
71	    printf '%s\n' "$g"
72	}
73	
74	# rate-limited action (60 s cooldown, never executed under DRY_RUN)
75	act() {
76	    local now=$SECONDS
77	    if [ $((now - LAST_ACT)) -lt 60 ]; then
78	        log "SKIP (cooldown) $*"
79	        return 0
80	    fi
81	    LAST_ACT=$now
82	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
83	        log "DRY_RUN would run: $*"
84	        return 0
85	    fi
86	    log "ACTION $*"
87	    "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1
88	    return 0
89	}
90	
91	resolve() {
92	    CUR=$(active_con)
93	    CUR_GW=""
94	    if [ -n "$CUR" ]; then
95	        CUR_GW=$(con_gw "$CUR")
96	        [ -z "$CUR_GW" ] && [ "$CUR" = "$CON" ] && CUR_GW="$PREF_GW"
97	    fi
98	}
99	
100	check_once() {

102	    resolve
103	    [ -n "$CUR_GW" ] && probe "$CUR_GW" && gw=up
104	    probe "$PROBE" && net=up
105	    echo "preferred_con=$CON preferred_dev=$DEV preferred_gw=$PREF_GW"
106	    echo "active_con=${CUR:-none} active_gw=${CUR_GW:-none} gw=$gw net=$net"
107	    echo "recovery_target=$CON"
108	}
109	
110	if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
111	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
112	    check_once
113	    exit 0
114	fi
115	
116	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
117	log "START pid=$$ dev=$DEV con=$CON pref_gw=$PREF_GW probe=$PROBE interval=${INTERVAL}s dry_run=$DRY_RUN"
118	
119	while :; do
120	    rotate
