Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

query.description: The search query to use

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

T = 16

STD = np.array([58.395, 57.12, 57.375], dtype=np.float32)


class _Log:
    def info(self, m):
        pass


def load_clip(path):
    vr = decord.VideoReader(path, num_threads=2)
    n = len(vr)
    idx = np.clip(((np.arange(T) + 0.5) * n / T).astype(int), 0, n - 1)

    for i, fr in enumerate(frames):
        h, w = fr.shape[:2]
        if h <= w:
            nh, nw = 256, max(256, int(round(w * 256 / h)))

        fr = fr[y0:y0 + 224, x0:x0 + 224]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Predicate/action phrase + verb-only ablation, encoded with X-CLIP text."""
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
import nltk

XCLIP = "/media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1/xyl/Display/EvcapProject/X-CLIP"
CKPT = os.path.join(XCLIP, "modelpth/k600_16_16.pth")
ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
AUX = {"is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "being", "has", "have", "had",
       "do", "does", "did", "can", "could", "will", "would", "should", "may",
       "might", "must", "s", "am"}
OBJ = {"DT", "JJ", "JJR", "JJS", "PRP$", "PRP", "NN", "NNS", "NNP", "NNPS", "CD"}
STOP = {"in", "on", "at", "to", "from", "with", "by", "for", "of", "into", "onto",
        "through", "across", "along", "around", "under", "near", "behind", "down",
        "up", "off", "over", "out", "during", "while", "as", "than", "about",
        "and", "or", "but", "that", "which", "who", "whom", "whose", "when", "where"}
SKIP = {"a", "an", "the", "this", "that", "these", "those", "his", "her", "their",
        "its", "my", "your", "our", "some", "any", "another", "each", "every"}


class _Log:
    def info(self, m):
        pass


def phrases_for(c):
    toks = [t.strip('.,!?;:"()') for t in c.split()]
    toks = [t for t in toks if t]
    tags = [t for _, t in nltk.pos_tag(toks)]
    vi = next((i for i, t in enumerate(tags) if t.startswith("VB") and toks[i].lower() not in AUX), None)
    if vi is None:
        return "", ""
    verb = toks[vi].lower()
    verb_only = verb
    out = [verb]
    j = vi + 1
    if j < len(toks) and tags[j] == "RP":
        out.append(toks[j].lower()); j += 1
    if j < len(toks) and tags[j] in ("DT", "PRP$"):
        out.append(toks[j].lower()); j += 1
    k = 0
    while j < len(toks) and k < 3:
        w = toks[j].lower()
        if tags[j] in ("IN", "CC", "TO", "WDT", "WP", "WRB") or w in STOP:
            break
        if tags[j] in ("DT", "PRP$", "PRP", "CD") or w in SKIP:
            j += 1
            continue
        if w.isalpha():
            out.append(w); k += 1
        j += 1
    return " ".join(out), verb_only


def main():
    S = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/external_sims_full.json")))
    caps = sorted({c for v in S.values() for c in v[0]})
    pred, verb = [], []
    for c in caps:
        p, v = phrases_for(c)
        pred.append(p)
        verb.append(v)
    print("unique captions", len(caps), "pred_nonempty", sum(bool(x) for x in pred), flush=True)
    sys.path.insert(0, XCLIP)
    os.chdir(XCLIP)
    import clip
    from models import xclip_all as xclip
    sd = torch.load(CKPT, map_location="cpu")["model"]
    model = xclip.build_model(sd, T=16, droppath=0.0, use_checkpoint=False, logger=_Log(),
                              prompts_alpha=0.1, prompts_layers=2, use_cache=True,
                              mit_layers=1, text_batch_size=0).cuda().eval()

    def encode(phr, fallback):
        out = np.zeros((len(phr), 512), dtype=np.float16)
        bs = 512
        for s in range(0, len(phr), bs):
            batch = [("a person is " + x) if x else fallback for x in phr[s:s + bs]]
            toks = clip.tokenize(batch, context_length=77, cut=True).cuda()
            with torch.no_grad(), torch.cuda.amp.autocast():
                e = model.encode_text(toks)
            out[s:s + bs] = e.float().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float16)
        return out

    np.save(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/uar_action_emb_fp16.npy"), encode(pred, "a person is doing something"))
    np.save(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/uar_verbonly_emb_fp16.npy"), encode(verb, "a person is doing something"))
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/uar_action_meta.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump({"captions": caps, "phrases": pred, "verb_only": verb}, f)
    print("DONE", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FAITHFUL_V2 CF3/D3/H3 JSONs from v2 retrieval."""
import json
import os

import numpy as np

ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
S = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/external_v2_sims.json")))
D = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/external_v2_top20.json")))
R = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "external/external_v2_reranked.json")))
EMB = os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/videoufo_brief_text_fp16.npy")
IDS = os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/videoufo_brief_ids.txt")
ACT = os.path.join(ROOT, "external/uar_action_emb_fp16.npy")
ACTM = os.path.join(ROOT, "external/uar_action_meta.json")
XV = os.path.join(ROOT, "features/xclip_video")
Q = np.load(os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/msrvtt_test_video_xclip_faithful_v2_video_fp16.npy"))
QIDS = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/msrvtt_test_video_xclip_faithful_v2_ids.txt")).read().splitlines()
qpos = {q: i for i, q in enumerate(QIDS)}
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "external")
ids = open(IDS).read().splitlines(); id2row = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(ids)}
E = np.load(EMB, mmap_mode="r"); A = np.load(ACT)
ameta = json.load(open(ACTM)); apos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(ameta["captions"])}


def z(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, np.float32); s = x.std()
    return np.zeros_like(x) if s < 1e-8 else np.clip((x - x.mean()) / s, -3, 3)


cf3, cf3s, d3, d3s, h3, h3s = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
for key, (caps, rels) in S.items():
    cf3[key] = [caps[:3], [0.0] * 3, [x["clip_ids"] for x in D[key][:3]]]
    cf3s[key] = [caps[:3], rels[:3]]
    rc = R[key][0][:3]; rq = R[key][1][:3]; rl = R[key][2][:3]
    d3[key] = [rc, rq, rl]
    m = {c: s for c, s in zip(caps, rels)}
    d3s[key] = [rc, [m.get(c, 0.0) for c in rc]]

    q = key.split("/")[-1][:-4]; n = len(caps)
    tv, gv, src, lists = [], [], [], []
    for j in range(n):
        cid = D[key][j]["clip_ids"][0]; row = id2row[cid]
        t = np.asarray(E[row], np.float32); tn = t / (np.linalg.norm(t) + 1e-8)
        tv.append(tn)
        vp = os.path.join(XV, cid + ".npy")
        if os.path.exists(vp):
            v = np.load(vp).astype(np.float32); gv.append(float(np.dot(v / (np.linalg.norm(v) + 1e-8), tn)))
        else:
            gv.append(0.0)
        src.append(cid.rsplit(".", 1)[0]); lists.append(D[key][j]["clip_ids"])
    capmat = np.stack(tv) @ np.stack(tv).T
    qv = Q[qpos[q]].astype(np.float32); qv = qv / (np.linalg.norm(qv) + 1e-8)
    act = np.array([(float(np.dot(qv, A[apos[c]].astype(np.float32) / (np.linalg.norm(A[apos[c]].astype(np.float32)) + 1e-8)))
                     if ameta["phrases"][apos[c]] else 0.0) for c in caps], np.float32)
    U = (z(rels) + z(act) + z(gv)) / 3
    chosen, cs = [], set()
    for _ in range(3):
        best, bi = -1e9, -1
        for i in range(n):
            if i in chosen: continue
            red = 0.0
            if chosen:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Paired bootstrap/permutation and per-query distribution for H5 vs baselines."""
import json
import os
import random
import sys

ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/evaluation"))
from pycocoevalcap.cider.cider import Cider  # noqa: E402

DIRS = {"H5": "eval_dev300_UARH5", "H7": "eval_dev300_UARH7",
        "D": "eval_dev300_D", "CF": "eval_dev300_CF",
        "D100k": "eval_dev300_D100k", "B": "eval_dev300_B"}
NAME = "eval_evcap_top7_bs1_load_video_feature_sim_score_cross_fusion_gate_not_share_linear_prompt5_review_generated_captions.json"


def load(d):
    p = os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/outputs", d, NAME)
    data = json.load(open(p))
    return {x["image_name"]: x["prediction"].strip() for x in data}


def main():
    P = {k: load(v) for k, v in DIRS.items()}
    GT = {}
    for line in open(os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/dev300/dev300.caption.tsv")):
        p = line.split("\t", 1)
        GT[p[0].split("/")[-1][:-4]] = [x["caption"] for x in json.loads(p[1])]
    K = list(P["H5"])
    g = {k: GT[k.split("/")[-1][:-4]] for k in K}
    sc = {m: dict(zip(K, Cider().compute_score(g, {k: [P[m][k]] for k in K})[1])) for m in P}

    rng = random.Random(42)
    out = {}
    for base in ["D", "CF", "D100k", "B"]:
        d = [sc["H5"][k] - sc[base][k] for k in K]
        obs = sum(d) / len(d)
        boots = []
        for _ in range(10000):
            s = [d[rng.randrange(len(d))] for _ in range(len(d))]
            boots.append(sum(s) / len(s))
        boots.sort()
        ci = (boots[250], boots[9750])
        # sign-flip permutation
        cnt = 0
        for _ in range(10000):
            s = [x if rng.random() < 0.5 else -x for x in d]
            if abs(sum(s) / len(s)) >= abs(obs):
                cnt += 1
        pval = (cnt + 1) / 10001
        bins = {"gt+1": 0, "p0.2_1": 0, "pm0.2": 0, "m1_-0.2": 0, "lt-1": 0}
        for x in d:
            if x > 1: bins["gt+1"] += 1
            elif x > 0.2: bins["p0.2_1"] += 1
            elif x >= -0.2: bins["pm0.2"] += 1
            elif x >= -1: bins["m1_-0.2"] += 1
            else: bins["lt-1"] += 1
        entries = sorted(((sc["H5"][k] - sc[base][k], k) for k in K))
        out[base] = {"mean_diff": round(obs, 4), "ci95": [round(ci[0], 4), round(ci[1], 4)],
                     "p_perm": round(pval, 5), "bins": bins,
                     "worst20": [{"query": k, "diff": round(v, 4),
                                  "H5": P["H5"][k], "base": P[base][k],
                                  "GT": GT[k.split("/")[-1][:-4]][:3]} for v, k in entries[:20]],
                     "best20": [{"query": k, "diff": round(v, 4),
                                 "H5": P["H5"][k], "base": P[base][k],
                                 "GT": GT[k.split("/")[-1][:-4]][:3]} for v, k in entries[-20:]]}
        print(base, out[base]["mean_diff"], out[base]["ci95"], out[base]["p_perm"], bins, flush=True)
    json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(ROOT, "reports/phase3_stats.json"), "w"), indent=1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--result_file_path", type=str, help="the result file to evaluate")
    #by lijian
    parser.add_argument('--eval_file', default = 'outputs/eval_evcap/000.josn')
    return parser.parse_args()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    args = parse_config()
    cocoEval = COCOEvalCap(args.result_file_path)
    cocoEval.evaluate()
            
    for metric, score in cocoEval.eval.items():
        print ('%s: %.3f'%(metric, score))
        
    # by lijian
    outfile = args.eval_file
    print(f'cocoeval outfile: {outfile}')
    with open(outfile, 'w') as fp:
        json.dump(cocoEval.eval, fp, indent=4)

# VideoUFO external-retrieval research workspace

Frozen 2026-11-19. Read-only inputs live on the 8 TB ext4 volume which is
currently mounted `ro`; every artifact produced here is on the home NVMe.

## Layout

```
manifests/     nested corpus manifests (10k .. full) + stats + SHA256SUMS
embeddings/    X-CLIP features
  videoufo_brief_text_fp16.npy        1,091,712 x 512 fp16 caption features
  videoufo_brief_ids.txt              row order (same as VideoUFO.csv data rows)
  msrvtt_test_video_fp16.npy          2,990 x 512 MSR-VTT test query features
  msrvtt_test_imgfeat_fp16.npy        2,990 x 196 x 512 frame-token features
indexes/       FAISS flat + IVF4096 over the full caption corpus
scripts/       manifest builder, feature extractors, retrieval sanity
retrieval/     top-20 sanity outputs
logs/
```

## Method note (important)

The paper (Displays 93 (2026) 103420, §3.3) retrieves **captions** with X-CLIP
(video-to-text).  The corpus is a text corpus; corpus videos are not embedded

retrieval artifact.  Corpus video features are only needed for the cross-gating

# UARCap — Utility-Aware Retrieval for Video Captioning

Research workspace for **large-scale external retrieval for video captioning**,
built on top of the EVCap codebase. The original EVCap checkpoint, prompts and
evaluation protocol are used as the fixed captioning baseline; no new captioning
module is trained in this repository.

- Baseline paper / code: EVCap: "Retrieval-augmented captioning with video-text
  features" (Displays 93 (2026) 103420) and its public implementation.
- External corpus: **VideoUFO** (200 tar shards, 1,091,712 clips, 93 parquet
  metadata files, CC BY 4.0), mounted read-only from the 8 TB volume.

## What this repository contains

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `manifests/` | Frozen nested corpus manifests `clips_{10k,50k,100k,250k,500k,full}.tsv`, `manifest_stats.json`, `SHA256SUMS` |
| `scripts/` | Manifest builder, X-CLIP / Video-LLaMA feature extractors, retrieval builders, UAR builders, metric and bootstrap scripts |
| `retrieval/` | Phase-1 top-20 retrieval outputs (raw + exact rescoring) per corpus scale |
| `external/` | Phase-2/3 external-retrieval results: similarity/rerank/top-20 JSON, UAR variant selections, selected clip lists, action-phrase metadata |
| `reports/` | Phase reports, failure taxonomy, oracle diagnostics, paired-statistics JSON |
| `evcap_external/` | Writable copy of EVCap with our patches: external-retrieval hooks, deterministic clip selection, no-retrieval mode, faithful preprocessing extractors, dev300 / val497 dataset configs |
| `PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC/` | Provenance labels for results produced before the FAITHFUL_V2 preprocessing fixes (numbers in `reports/` predating the fix) |

## What is deliberately **not** in the repository

Git history must stay small and free of raw data. Excluded (see `.gitignore`):

- VideoUFO videos and metadata (datasets, `*.mp4`, `*.parquet`)
- X-CLIP / Video-LLaMA / EVCap weights (`*.pt`, `*.pth`, `*.bin`, `*.safetensors`)
- Embeddings and feature caches (`embeddings/`, `features/`, `*.npy`, `*.npz`)
- FAISS indexes (`indexes/`, `*.faiss`, `*.index`)
- Raw frame tables (`*.img.tsv`, 138 MB for dev300 alone)
- SPICE cache, Stanford CoreNLP jars/models, METEOR paraphrase data, third-party
  demo assets and the vendored EgoInstructor repository
- Run logs, checkpoints symlinked from the read-only disk, `__pycache__`

Generated captions (`*_generated_captions.json`) and `metrics.json` **are**
kept: they are small and are the actual experimental record.

## Research phases

1. **Phase 1 — external retrieval.** Audit EVCap, freeze nested VideoUFO
   manifests, extract X-CLIP caption features for 1,091,712 clips, build FAISS
   indexes, retrieve top-20 for 300 dev queries, sanity-check oracle recall.
2. **Phase 2 — scale study.** Retrieval at 10K / 100K / 500K / FULL with the
   same query set; naive external retrieval (CF), quality reranking (D), and
   paired per-query analysis against the paper baseline (B) and no-retrieval (A).
3. **Phase 3 — UAR.** Training-free Utility-Aware Reranking combining
   `S_relevance`, `S_action`, `S_grounding` and redundancy control, with fixed-k
   and adaptive-k variants (E/F/Fv/G/H/H1/H3/H5/H7/I), validated with paired
   bootstrap/permutation tests.
4. **FAITHFUL_V2 — preprocessing fidelity.** Two confirmed deviations were fixed
   before any new claims: MSR-VTT X-CLIP query resize switched
   `INTER_LINEAR → INTER_NEAREST` (official X-CLIP protocol), and VideoUFO
   Video-LLaMA fusion features switched to a fixed faithful temporal sampling
   (`linspace(0, N-1, 16)`). Query features were re-extracted under
   `*_xclip_faithful_v2*`, FULL retrieval recomputed, and CF3/D3/H3 rerun for a
   like-for-like comparison. Results produced before the fix are prefixed
   `PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC` and must not be mixed with FAITHFUL_V2 numbers.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. corpus manifests (deterministic: source-hash order, round-robin by topic)
python3 scripts/build_manifests.py

# 2. X-CLIP caption embeddings for the VideoUFO brief captions
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/extract_text_embeddings.py

# 3. MSR-VTT query features (FAITHFUL_V2: 16 center frames, INTER_NEAREST)
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/extract_query_features_v2.py \
    <test.label.tsv> msrvtt_test_video_xclip_faithful_v2

# 4. FAISS index + retrieval sanity
/media/.../repro_evcap/venv/bin/python scripts/build_faiss_index.py
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/retrieval_sanity.py

# 5. external retrieval / UAR json
python3 scripts/make_external_retrieval_v2.py
python3 scripts/build_v2_variants.py

# 6. generation + metrics (needs EVCap checkpoint + Vicuna weights, not in repo)
bash scripts/run_v2.sh CF3v2   # likewise D3v2, H3v2
bash scripts/run_metrics.sh <generated_captions.json> <metrics.json>
```

`extract_msrvtt_query_features.py` must import torch before cv2 (OpenMP
conflict otherwise: cv2-before-torch segfaults at `model.cuda()`).

### Rebuilding the large manifests

`manifests/*.tsv` are generated from `VideoUFO.csv` plus the frozen manifest
builder: source-hash ordering, round-robin within topic, proportional topic
allocation, strict nesting. `manifests/manifest_stats.json` records row counts,
topic distribution and nesting checks; `manifests/SHA256SUMS` pins the exact
files. If a checkout ever lacks the large TSVs, rerunning `build_manifests.py`
on the same `VideoUFO.csv` reproduces them byte-identically (verified by
`SHA256SUMS`).

# UARCap — Utility-Aware Retrieval for Video Captioning

Research workspace for **large-scale external retrieval for video captioning**,
built on top of the EVCap codebase. The original EVCap checkpoint, prompts and
evaluation protocol are used as the fixed captioning baseline; no new captioning
module is trained in this repository.

- Baseline paper / code: EVCap: "Retrieval-augmented captioning with video-text
  features" (Displays 93 (2026) 103420) and its public implementation.
- External corpus: **VideoUFO** (200 tar shards, 1,091,712 clips, 93 parquet
  metadata files, CC BY 4.0), mounted read-only from the 8 TB volume.

## What this repository contains

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `manifests/` | Frozen nested corpus manifests `clips_{10k,50k,100k,250k,500k,full}.tsv`, `manifest_stats.json`, `SHA256SUMS` |
| `scripts/` | Manifest builder, X-CLIP / Video-LLaMA feature extractors, retrieval builders, UAR builders, metric and bootstrap scripts |
| `retrieval/` | Phase-1 top-20 retrieval outputs (raw + exact rescoring) per corpus scale |
| `external/` | Phase-2/3 external-retrieval results: similarity/rerank/top-20 JSON, UAR variant selections, selected clip lists, action-phrase metadata |
| `reports/` | Phase reports, failure taxonomy, oracle diagnostics, paired-statistics JSON |
| `evcap_external/` | Writable copy of EVCap with our patches: external-retrieval hooks, deterministic clip selection, no-retrieval mode, faithful preprocessing extractors, dev300 / val497 dataset configs |
| `PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC/` | Provenance labels for results produced before the FAITHFUL_V2 preprocessing fixes (numbers in `reports/` predating the fix) |

## What is deliberately **not** in the repository

Git history must stay small and free of raw data. Excluded (see `.gitignore`):

- VideoUFO videos and metadata (datasets, `*.mp4`, `*.parquet`)
- X-CLIP / Video-LLaMA / EVCap weights (`*.pt`, `*.pth`, `*.bin`, `*.safetensors`)
- Embeddings and feature caches (`embeddings/`, `features/`, `*.npy`, `*.npz`)
- FAISS indexes (`indexes/`, `*.faiss`, `*.index`)
- Raw frame tables (`*.img.tsv`, 138 MB for dev300 alone)
- SPICE cache, Stanford CoreNLP jars/models, METEOR paraphrase data, third-party
  demo assets and the vendored EgoInstructor repository
- Run logs, checkpoints symlinked from the read-only disk, `__pycache__`

Generated captions (`*_generated_captions.json`) and `metrics.json` **are**
kept: they are small and are the actual experimental record.

## Research phases

1. **Phase 1 — external retrieval.** Audit EVCap, freeze nested VideoUFO
   manifests, extract X-CLIP caption features for 1,091,712 clips, build FAISS
   indexes, retrieve top-20 for 300 dev queries, sanity-check oracle recall.
2. **Phase 2 — scale study.** Retrieval at 10K / 100K / 500K / FULL with the
   same query set; naive external retrieval (CF), quality reranking (D), and
   paired per-query analysis against the paper baseline (B) and no-retrieval (A).
3. **Phase 3 — UAR.** Training-free Utility-Aware Reranking combining
   `S_relevance`, `S_action`, `S_grounding` and redundancy control, with fixed-k
   and adaptive-k variants (E/F/Fv/G/H/H1/H3/H5/H7/I), validated with paired
   bootstrap/permutation tests.
4. **FAITHFUL_V2 — preprocessing fidelity.** Two confirmed deviations were fixed
   before any new claims: MSR-VTT X-CLIP query resize switched
   `INTER_LINEAR → INTER_NEAREST` (official X-CLIP protocol), and VideoUFO
   Video-LLaMA fusion features switched to a fixed faithful temporal sampling
   (`linspace(0, N-1, 16)`). Query features were re-extracted under
   `*_xclip_faithful_v2*`, FULL retrieval recomputed, and CF3/D3/H3 rerun for a
   like-for-like comparison. Results produced before the fix are prefixed
   `PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC` and must not be mixed with FAITHFUL_V2 numbers.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. corpus manifests (deterministic: source-hash order, round-robin by topic)
python3 scripts/build_manifests.py

# 2. X-CLIP caption embeddings for the VideoUFO brief captions
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/extract_text_embeddings.py

# 3. MSR-VTT query features (FAITHFUL_V2: 16 center frames, INTER_NEAREST)
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/extract_query_features_v2.py \
    <test.label.tsv> msrvtt_test_video_xclip_faithful_v2

# 4. FAISS index + retrieval sanity
/media/.../repro_evcap/venv/bin/python scripts/build_faiss_index.py
/home/bn/anaconda3/envs/videollama2/bin/python scripts/retrieval_sanity.py

# 5. external retrieval / UAR json
python3 scripts/make_external_retrieval_v2.py
python3 scripts/build_v2_variants.py

# 6. generation + metrics (needs EVCap checkpoint + Vicuna weights, not in repo)
bash scripts/run_v2.sh CF3v2   # likewise D3v2, H3v2
bash scripts/run_metrics.sh <generated_captions.json> <metrics.json>
```

`extract_msrvtt_query_features.py` must import torch before cv2 (OpenMP
conflict otherwise: cv2-before-torch segfaults at `model.cuda()`).

### Rebuilding the large manifests

`manifests/*.tsv` are generated from `VideoUFO.csv` plus the frozen manifest
builder: source-hash ordering, round-robin within topic, proportional topic
allocation, strict nesting. `manifests/manifest_stats.json` records row counts,
topic distribution and nesting checks; `manifests/SHA256SUMS` pins the exact
files. If a checkout ever lacks the large TSVs, rerunning `build_manifests.py`
on the same `VideoUFO.csv` reproduces them byte-identically (verified by
`SHA256SUMS`).

## Notes on retrieval protocol

EVCap §3.3 retrieves **captions** with X-CLIP (video-to-text); corpus videos are
never embedded for retrieval. The 1,091,712 VideoUFO caption features are the
faithful retrieval artifact. Corpus video features (Video-LLaMA 32×768) are only
needed for cross-gating fusion of the top-K retrieved clips and are computed on
demand under `features/`.

The paper reports MSR-VTT 86.69 / 50.11 / 32.47 / 66.64 / 72.20 and MSVD
91.53 / 69.67 / 47.04 / 84.04 / 158.32 (B@1/B@4/M/R/CIDEr, ×100).

## Status

Phase 1–2 complete; Phase 3 UAR complete on PRE_FIX features; FAITHFUL_V2
preprocessing fixes applied and the CF3/D3/H3 comparison rerun in progress.
Numbers under `reports/` that predate the fix are explicitly marked
`PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC` and are not paper claims.

# VideoUFO external-retrieval research workspace

Frozen 2026-11-19. Read-only inputs live on the 8 TB ext4 volume which is
currently mounted `ro`; every artifact produced here is on the home NVMe.

## Layout

```
manifests/     nested corpus manifests (10k .. full) + stats + SHA256SUMS
embeddings/    X-CLIP features
  videoufo_brief_text_fp16.npy        1,091,712 x 512 fp16 caption features
  videoufo_brief_ids.txt              row order (same as VideoUFO.csv data rows)
  msrvtt_test_video_fp16.npy          2,990 x 512 MSR-VTT test query features
  msrvtt_test_imgfeat_fp16.npy        2,990 x 196 x 512 frame-token features
indexes/       FAISS flat + IVF4096 over the full caption corpus
scripts/       manifest builder, feature extractors, retrieval sanity
retrieval/     top-20 sanity outputs
logs/
```

## Method note (important)

The paper (Displays 93 (2026) 103420, §3.3) retrieves **captions** with X-CLIP
(video-to-text).  The corpus is a text corpus; corpus videos are not embedded
for retrieval.  The 1.09M VideoUFO caption features are therefore the faithful
retrieval artifact.  Corpus video features are only needed for the cross-gating
fusion stage, and only for the top-K retrieved clips (Video-LLaMA 32x768),
computed on demand and cached.

# FAITHFUL_V2 — preprocessing fix, pre/post retrieval overlap, CF3/D3/H3 rerun

Date: 2026-11-19. dev300, 300 queries, same EVCap checkpoint, deterministic decoding.

## 1. Confirmed preprocessing deviations and fixes

| Path | PRE_FIX_DIAGNOSTIC | FAITHFUL_V2 |
|---|---|---|
| MSR-VTT query X-CLIP resize | `cv2.INTER_LINEAR` | `cv2.INTER_NEAREST` (official X-CLIP) |
| VideoUFO Video-LLaMA fusion frames | center-of-bin (16 center frames) | `linspace(0, N-1, 16)` endpoints |
| Frames / size / norm / checkpoint | 16, 224, ImageNet, same ckpt | unchanged |

New artifacts: `embeddings/msrvtt_test_video_xclip_faithful_v2_*`,
`features/videollama_faithful_v2/` (1,781 clips, 0 decode failures),
`external/external_v2_{sims,top20,reranked}.json`.

## 2. Pre/post FULL retrieval overlap (dev300)

| Metric | PRE_FIX | FAITHFUL_V2 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| top1 caption changed | — | 152/300 = 50.7% | — |
| top20 set overlap | — | 0.6222 | — |
| top3 set overlap | — | 0.5411 | — |
| top1 similarity | 0.2820 | 0.2782 | −0.0038 |
| top20 mean similarity | 0.2686 | 0.2645 | −0.0041 |
| oracle@20 (CIDEr) | 0.2189 | 0.2155 | −0.0034 |
| oracle@7 | 0.1548 | 0.1596 | +0.0048 |
| oracle@3 | 0.1142 | 0.1154 | +0.0012 |
| top1 caption CIDEr | 0.0762 | 0.0753 | −0.0009 |
| rerank top1 CIDEr | 0.0981 | 0.1005 | +0.0024 |

The fix reshuffles candidates substantially but leaves retrieval quality flat.

Action-phrase coverage had to be rebuilt over the union of PRE_FIX + v2 + val497
captions (14,641 strings) because v2 introduced ~9k unseen captions; otherwise
`KeyError` or silent zero action scores.

X-CLIP grounding features were completed for all v2-selected clips
(297 newly fetched); after that S_grounding changed the UAR selection
(1,780 → 1,752 clips).

## 3. Six metrics (×100)

| | B1 | B4 | M | R-L | CIDEr | SPICE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CF3v2 | 86.33 | 46.66 | 31.83 | 64.69 | 65.57 | 8.49 |
| D3v2 | 85.95 | 47.62 | 32.53 | 65.11 | **67.09** | **8.77** |
| H3v2 | 86.17 | 46.96 | 32.22 | 64.94 | 66.32 | 8.62 |
| H3 (PRE_FIX) | 87.10 | 48.29 | 32.28 | 65.09 | 67.63 | 8.77 |
| D7 (PRE_FIX) | 84.33 | 44.42 | 31.59 | 63.98 | 63.25 | 8.55 |
| CF7 (PRE_FIX) | 85.15 | 45.42 | 31.80 | 64.19 | 64.38 | 8.77 |

## 4. Paired per-query CIDEr differences (10k bootstrap, 10k sign-flip permutation)

| Comparison | Δ CIDEr | 95% CI | p | W/L |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H3v2 − CF3v2 | +0.75 | [−1.0, +2.8] | 0.472 | 32/35 |
| H3v2 − D3v2 | −0.77 | [−2.7, +1.1] | 0.429 | 47/53 |
| H3v2 − H3pre | −1.31 | [−3.3, +0.6] | 0.196 | 31/44 |
| H3v2 − CF7 | +1.94 | [−0.4, +4.5] | 0.133 | 60/53 |
| H3v2 − D7 | +3.07 | [+0.3, +5.9] | **0.032** | 78/59 |
| D3v2 − CF3v2 | +1.52 | [−0.7, +4.1] | — | — |

## 5. Conclusion

Under the faithful preprocessing and the like-for-like k=3 comparison, the
PRE_FIX H3 advantage does **not** reproduce: H3v2 (66.32) is numerically below
D3v2 (67.09) and statistically indistinguishable from both D3v2 and CF3v2.
The PRE_FIX 67.63 was not solely a preprocessing artifact (H3v2 − H3pre = −1.31,
p=0.20), but the gain over reranking-only (D) is gone, and even D3v2 − CF3v2 is
not significant. Therefore the previous claim "H3 > D" is withdrawn; the k=3
regime is dominated by candidate-set quality, with no measurable UAR gain at
this sample size.

Do not run E/F/G component ablations for a "win" until a k>3 or larger dev set
shows a reproducible H−D gap.

## FAITHFUL_V2 结果（dev300，300 查询，同 checkpoint，deterministic）

### 六指标（×100）

| | B1 | B4 | M | R-L | CIDEr | SPICE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CF3v2 | 86.33 | 46.66 | 31.83 | 64.69 | 65.57 | 8.49 |
| D3v2 | 85.95 | **47.62** | **32.53** | **65.11** | **67.09** | **8.77** |
| H3v2 | 86.17 | 46.96 | 32.22 | 64.94 | 66.32 | 8.62 |
| H3 PRE_FIX | 87.10 | 48.29 | 32.28 | 65.09 | 67.63 | 8.77 |
| D7 PRE_FIX | 84.33 | 44.42 | 31.59 | 63.98 | 63.25 | 8.55 |

### 配对 bootstrap（CIDEr，10000 次，sign-flip permutation）

| 比较 | Δ | 95% CI | p | 胜负 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H3v2 − CF3v2 | +0.75 | [−1.0, +2.8] | 0.472 | 32/35 |
| **H3v2 − D3v2** | **−0.77** | **[−2.7, +1.1]** | **0.429** | 47/53 |
| H3v2 − H3pre | −1.31 | [−3.3, +0.6] | 0.196 | 31/44 |
| H3v2 − CF7 | +1.94 | [−0.4, +4.5] | 0.133 | 60/53 |
| H3v2 − D7 | +3.07 | [+0.3, +5.9] | **0.032** | 78/59 |
| D3v2 − CF3v2 | +1.52 | [−0.7, +4.1] | — | — |

### 结论（与 pre-fix 相比发生了实质性变化）

1. **预处理修正本身是“中性”的**：top1 改变 50.7%、top20 重叠 62.2%，但 oracle@3/7/20、top1/rerank CIDEr 全部在 ±0.005 内。
2. **H3 的核心增益没有复现**：faithful 下 H3v2 = 66.32，低于 D3v2 = 67.09；配对差 −0.77，CI 跨 0，p = 0.43。之前 “H3 显著优于 D” 的结论**必须撤回**。
3. H3v2 相对自身 pre-fix 只降 1.31（p = 0.20），说明 67.63 并非纯预处理假象，但 **k=7→3 的原方法对照补齐后，增益被 D 基线吸收**。
4. 连 **D3v2 − CF3v2（+1.52）也不显著**：在 k=3 下候选集质量主导，UAR 与 ROUGE 重排都没有可测出的增量。
5. 唯一仍显著的是 H3v2 − D7（+3.07，p = 0.032），但这是 k=3 vs k=7 的上下文长度效应，不是 UAR 贡献。

按你的指令，E/F/G 组件消融**暂不重跑** —— 在 k=3、300 查询下没有可复现的 H−D gap，继续拆组件只会得到噪声。

产物：`reports/faithful_v2.md`、`reports/v2_stats.json`、三组 `generated_captions.json` + `metrics.json`。已按约定提交并 push：`1b6942d`（`exp: FAITHFUL_V2 CF3/D3/H3 rerun + paired statistics`），push 成功。

下一步建议（需你确认）：把 k 恢复到 5/7 重跑 faithful 的 H vs D，或直接在 official val497 上做方法选择——只有 val 上出现可复现 gap，才值得进 untouched test。

paths = ids(os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/val497/val_video_paths.tsv"))

def load_clip(path):
    vr = decord.VideoReader(path, num_threads=2)
    n = len(vr)
    idx = np.clip(((np.arange(T) + 0.5) * n / T).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
    frames = vr.get_batch(idx).asnumpy()
    o = np.empty((T, 224, 224, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    for i, fr in enumerate(frames):
        h, w = fr.shape[:2]
        if h <= w:
            nh, nw = 256, max(256, int(round(w * 256 / h)))

        fr = cv2.resize(fr, (nw, nh), interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)

        o[i] = (fr[y0:y0 + 224, x0:x0 + 224].astype(np.float32) - MEAN) / STD

  ImageNet norm — `features/videollama_faithful_v2/`.

| k | CF oracle@k | D oracle@k | CF gen CIDEr | D gen CIDEr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0800 | 0.1176 | 53.20 | 51.77 |
| 3 | 0.1314 | 0.1481 | 52.42 | **53.14** |
| 5 | 0.1535 | 0.1720 | 51.29 | 50.51 |
| 7 | 0.1698 | 0.1835 | 51.13 | 50.05 |

Coverage increases monotonically with k for both orderings, while generation
utility does not: CF peaks at k=1 and declines; D peaks at k=3 and then falls
sharply. This is the inverted-U / context-overload pattern on an independent
split.

## 3. Paired per-query CIDEr (10k bootstrap, 10k sign-flip)

| Comparison | Δ CIDEr | 95% CI | p | W/L/T |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D3 − D7 | **+3.11** | [+0.72, +5.70] | **0.012** | 112/88/297 |
| D3 − D5 | **+2.65** | [+0.64, +4.78] | **0.012** | 92/62/343 |
| D5 − D7 | +0.46 | [−1.14, +2.13] | 0.583 | 88/72/337 |
| D1 − D3 | −1.38 | [−3.62, +0.73] | 0.229 | 85/96/316 |
| CF1 − CF7 | +2.11 | [−0.36, +4.66] | 0.098 | 125/123/249 |
| CF1 − CF3 | +0.78 | [−1.06, +2.72] | 0.421 | 94/86/317 |
| CF3 − CF7 | +1.33 | [−0.92, +3.60] | 0.252 | 111/114/272 |
| CF5 − CF7 | +0.19 | [−1.70, +2.11] | 0.843 | 89/84/324 |
| D3 − CF3 | +0.74 | [−1.53, +3.03] | 0.544 | 104/93/300 |
| D3 − CF1 | −0.05 | [−2.37, +2.36] | 0.966 | 111/106/280 |
| D7 − CF7 | −1.04 | [−3.47, +1.35] | 0.392 | 104/106/287 |

`D3 > D5` and `D3 > D7` are the only significant effects; the ordering (CF vs D)
does not matter at the optimum (D3 vs CF1 indistinguishable).

## 4. Tie structure (important)

Because beam search is deterministic and many queries ignore the extra context,
a large fraction of outputs is identical across k:

| Pair | identical generated captions |
|---|---|
| D3 vs D7 | 295/497 (59.4%) |
| CF3 vs CF7 | 271/497 (54.5%) |
| D3 vs CF3 | 300/497 (60.4%) |
| D1 vs D3 | 316/497 (63.6%) |

On the queries where output actually changes, the effect is much larger:
D3 − D7 = **+7.64** CIDEr (202 queries), CF3 − CF7 = **+2.93** (226 queries).
The aggregate +3.11 / +1.33 are diluted by the 55–60% identical outputs.
Any future contextual method must be judged on changed-query behavior, and
context sensitivity itself is a meaningful signal for adaptive budgeting.

## 5. Conclusion

`context-overload finding reproduces on the independent validation split`:

- candidate coverage rises with k (oracle@1 → oracle@7: CF 0.080→0.170, D 0.118→0.184);
- generation utility peaks at k=3 for quality reranking (D3 = 53.14, significantly
  above D5 and D7, p = 0.012) and at k=1 for raw retrieval (CF1 = 53.20);
- the two optima are statistically indistinguishable (D3 − CF1 = −0.05, p = 0.97);
- the apparent dev300 optimum k=3 is corroborated for D, while raw CF does not
  benefit from any additional context.

Therefore the second-round method is justified: **Adaptive Context Budgeting**
(decide how much retrieved context each query receives), not another reranking
score. All thresholds/stopping policies must be fit on val497 only; the
untouched test2690 is for final evaluation, full test2990 for paper comparison.

特征只用 caption redundancy/source duplication。

## J4. Quality-tail stopping

如果后续 D-rerank caption quality 明显下降，
停止。

设计一个非常简单、可解释的边际 evidence score，例如：

m_i =
a * normalized relevance_i
+ b * normalized quality_i
+ c * grounding_i
- d * redundancy_i
- e * same_source_i

OOF adaptive − D3 ≥ +1.0 CIDEr

OOF gain ≥ +0.5 CIDEr

"""Step F: per-query oracle context budget on val497 (no GPU, no regeneration)."""
import json
import os
import random
import sys

ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/outputs")
NAME = "eval_evcap_top7_bs1_load_video_feature_sim_score_cross_fusion_gate_not_share_linear_prompt5_review_generated_captions.json"
KS = [1, 3, 5, 7]
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "evcap_external/evaluation"))
from pycocoevalcap.cider.cider import Cider  # noqa: E402


def caps(k):
    d = f"eval_val497_D{k}"
    return {x["image_name"]: x["prediction"].strip() for x in json.load(open(os.path.join(OUT, d, NAME)))}


GT = {}
for line in open("/media/bn/37b77782-9321-42a0-8a20-f53b4ec9179d1/xyl/Display/lj/datasets/MSRVTT-v2/val.caption.tsv"):
    p = line.split("\t", 1)

P = {k: caps(k) for k in KS}

g = {q: GT[q.split("/")[-1][:-4]] for q in Q}
C = {}
for k in KS:
    C[k] = dict(zip(Q, Cider().compute_score(g, {q: [P[k][q]] for q in Q})[1]))

star = []
for q in Q:
    vals = [C[k][q] for k in KS]

dist = {k: star.count(k) for k in KS}
fixed = {k: sum(C[k][q] for q in Q) / len(Q) for k in KS}
best_fixed_k = max(KS, key=lambda k: fixed[k])
oracle = sum(max(C[k][q] for k in KS) for q in Q) / len(Q)
ident_all = sum(len({P[k][q] for k in KS}) == 1 for q in Q)
sens = len(Q) - ident_all

rng = random.Random(42)
boots = sorted(sum(d[rng.randrange(len(d))] for _ in range(len(d))) / len(d) for _ in range(10000))
ci = (boots[250], boots[9750])

out = {
    "queries": len(Q),
    "k_star_distribution": dist,
    "k_star_ratio": {k: round(dist[k] / len(Q), 4) for k in KS},
    "fixed_mean_cider": {k: round(fixed[k], 4) for k in KS},
    "best_fixed_k": best_fixed_k,
    "oracle_adaptive_mean_cider": round(oracle, 4),
    "oracle_minus_best_fixed": round(oracle - fixed[best_fixed_k], 4),
    "oracle_minus_best_fixed_ci95": [round(ci[0], 4), round(ci[1], 4)],
    "all_k_identical_queries": ident_all,
    "context_sensitive_queries": sens,
}
json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(ROOT, "reports/oracle_budget_val497.json"), "w"), indent=2)
print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Step H: inference-time features for each val497 query (no GT used)."""
import json
import os

import numpy as np

ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
EXT = os.path.join(ROOT, "external")
S = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, "external_val_sims.json")))
R = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, "external_val_reranked.json")))
D = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, "external_val_top20.json")))
E = np.load(os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/videoufo_brief_text_fp16.npy"), mmap_mode="r")
IDS = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "embeddings/videoufo_brief_ids.txt")).read().splitlines()
id2row = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(IDS)}
XV = os.path.join(ROOT, "features/xclip_video")


def rouge_l(a, b):
    x, y = a.lower().split(), b.lower().split()
    if not x or not y:
        return 0.0
    dp = [[0] * (len(y) + 1) for _ in range(len(x) + 1)]
    for i in range(1, len(x) + 1):
        for j in range(1, len(y) + 1):
            dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 if x[i - 1] == y[j - 1] else max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    l = dp[-1][-1]
    if l == 0:
        return 0.0
    p, r = l / len(x), l / len(y)
    return 2 * p * r / (p + r)


def emb(cid):
    return np.asarray(E[id2row[cid]], np.float32)


rows = {}
for key in S:
    q = key.split("/")[-1][:-4]
    sims = S[key][1][:7]
    rc, rq, rl = R[key][0][:7], R[key][1][:7], R[key][2][:7]
    feats = {}
    for i in (1, 2, 3, 5, 7):
        feats[f"sim{i}"] = float(sims[i - 1])
    feats["sim1-sim2"] = sims[0] - sims[1]
    feats["sim1-sim3"] = sims[0] - sims[2]
    feats["sim3-sim5"] = sims[2] - sims[4]
    feats["sim5-sim7"] = sims[4] - sims[6]
    for k in (3, 5, 7):
        a = np.array(sims[:k]); feats[f"sim_mean{k}"] = float(a.mean()); feats[f"sim_std{k}"] = float(a.std())
    adj = np.diff(np.array(sims))
    feats["sim_max_adjacent_gap"] = float(np.max(adj))
    feats["sim_gap_pos"] = int(np.argmax(adj) + 1)  # gap after position g
    feats["sim_rel_decay"] = float((sims[0] - sims[6]) / (sims[0] + 1e-8))
    for i in (1, 2, 3, 5, 7):
        feats[f"q{i}"] = float(rq[i - 1])
    feats["q1-q3"] = rq[0] - rq[2]
    feats["q3-q5"] = rq[2] - rq[4]
    feats["q5-q7"] = rq[4] - rq[6]
    qa = np.array(rq)
    feats["q_mean7"] = float(qa.mean()); feats["q_std7"] = float(qa.std())
    feats["q_disp7"] = float(qa.std() / (abs(qa.mean()) + 1e-8))

    cids = [lst[0] for lst in rl]
    em = np.stack([emb(c) for c in cids])
    em = em / (np.linalg.norm(em, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-8)
    cm = em @ em.T
    for k in (3, 5, 7):
        sub = cm[:k]
        iu = np.triu_indices(k, 1)
        feats[f"cap_cos_mean{k}"] = float(sub[iu].mean())
        feats[f"cap_cos_max{k}"] = float(sub[iu].max())
    feats["cap_cos_inc_1_3"] = feats["cap_cos_mean3"]
    feats["cap_cos_inc_3_5"] = feats["cap_cos_mean5"] - feats["cap_cos_mean3"]
    feats["cap_cos_inc_5_7"] = feats["cap_cos_mean7"] - feats["cap_cos_mean5"]

    def nd(cs):
        n = len(cs)
        if n < 2:
            return 0.0
        return sum(rouge_l(cs[i], cs[j]) >= 0.8 for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)) / (n * (n - 1) / 2)
    feats["near_dup7"] = nd(rc)
    feats["near_dup_inc_1_3"] = nd(rc[:3])
    feats["near_dup_inc_3_5"] = nd(rc[:5]) - nd(rc[:3])
    feats["near_dup_inc_5_7"] = nd(rc[:7]) - nd(rc[:5])
    srcs = [c.rsplit(".", 1)[0] for c in cids]
    feats["unique_sources7"] = len(set(srcs))
    feats["repeat_sources7"] = 7 - len(set(srcs))
    feats["source_div7"] = len(set(srcs)) / 7
    topics = [D[key][j].get("topics") for j in range(7)]
    feats["unique_topics7"] = len({str(t) for t in topics})

    gv, gv_ok = [], []
    for c, lst in zip(rc, rl):
        cid = lst[0]
        p = os.path.join(XV, cid + ".npy")
        t = emb(cid); t = t / (np.linalg.norm(t) + 1e-8)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            v = np.load(p).astype(np.float32); gv.append(float(np.dot(v / (np.linalg.norm(v) + 1e-8), t))); gv_ok.append(1)
        else:
            gv.append(0.0); gv_ok.append(0)
    ga = np.array(gv)
    feats["ground1"] = float(ga[0])
    for k in (3, 5, 7):
        feats[f"ground_mean{k}"] = float(ga[:k].mean())
    feats["ground_std7"] = float(ga.std())
    feats["ground_decay"] = float(ga[0] - ga[6])
    feats["ground_coverage"] = float(sum(gv_ok) / 7)
    rows[q] = feats

json.dump(rows, open(os.path.join(ROOT, "reports/val_budget_features.json"), "w"))
print("queries", len(rows), "features", len(next(iter(rows.values()))))

- D7

---

# 2. 这组实验的目的

验证：

**optimal context budget 是否会随 retrieval corpus scale 改变。**

这是当前论文非常重要的潜在结果。

- BLEU-4

- SPICE

# 3. 必须保证与 FULL val497 完全一致

- same INTER_NEAREST
- same checkpoint
- same prompt
- same seed
- same beam
- same D/ROUGE-L ranking
- same evaluation scripts
- same k semantics

def rouge_l(a, b):
    x, y = a.lower().split(), b.lower().split()
    if not x or not y:
        return 0.0
    dp = [[0] * (len(y) + 1) for _ in range(len(x) + 1)]
    for i in range(1, len(x) + 1):
        for j in range(1, len(y) + 1):
            dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 if x[i - 1] == y[j - 1] else max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    l = dp[-1][-1]
    if l == 0:
        return 0.0
    p, r = l / len(x), l / len(y)
    return 2 * p * r / (p + r)

    print("model loaded", flush=True)

    for k, q in enumerate(qids):
        qv = Q[k]
        img = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(QI[k], dtype=np.float32)).cuda().half().unsqueeze(0)
        bv = torch.full((TOPK,), -1e4, device="cuda")
        bi = torch.zeros(TOPK, dtype=torch.long, device="cuda")
        for s in range(0, len(order), CHUNK):
            tf = X[s:s + CHUNK].unsqueeze(0)
            with torch.no_grad(), torch.cuda.amp.autocast():
                tf = tf + model.prompts_generator(tf, img)
                sc = qv @ F.normalize(tf[0], dim=1).T
            v, i = torch.topk(sc, min(TOPK, sc.numel()))
            i = i + s
            av, ai = torch.cat([bv, v]), torch.cat([bi, i])
            bv, sel = torch.topk(av, TOPK)
            bi = ai[sel]
        caps = [order[i] for i in bi.cpu().tolist()]

        key = f"datasets/MSRVTT-v2/videos/{q}.mp4"

    for key, (caps, scores) in sims.items():

             for i in range(len(caps))]
        idx = sorted(range(len(caps)), key=lambda i: (-q[i], i))[:TOPN]
        rids = [groups[caps[i]] for i in idx]
        reranked[key] = [[caps[i] for i in idx], [q[i] for i in idx], rids]
        for lst in rids:
            top7.add(lst[0])
    json.dump(sims, open(os.path.join(OUT, "external_val_sims.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    json.dump(diag, open(os.path.join(OUT, "external_val_top20.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    json.dump(reranked, open(os.path.join(OUT, "external_val_reranked.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    open(os.path.join(OUT, "external_val_top7_clips.txt"), "w").write("\n".join(sorted(top7)) + "\n")
    print("DONE queries", len(sims), "top7", len(top7), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build val497 CF7/D7 cap+sim JSONs for a manifest scale.

Usage: build_val_grid_scale.py <scale>
Reads external/external_val_<scale>_{sims,top20,reranked}.json and writes
external/external_val_<scale>_{cf7,d7}_{cap,sims}.json + <scale>_grid_clips.txt.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

ROOT = "/home/bn/videoufo_research"
EXT = os.path.join(ROOT, "external")
SCALE = sys.argv[1]
S = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_sims.json")))
D = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_top20.json")))
R = json.load(open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_reranked.json")))

cf, cfs, dd, ds = {}, {}, {}, {}
for key, (caps, rels) in S.items():
    cf[key] = [caps[:7], rels[:7], [D[key][j]["clip_ids"] for j in range(7)]]
    cfs[key] = [caps[:7], rels[:7]]
    rc, rq, rl = R[key][0][:7], R[key][1][:7], R[key][2][:7]
    dd[key] = [rc, rq, rl]
    m = {c: s for c, s in zip(caps, rels)}
    ds[key] = [rc, [m.get(c, 0.0) for c in rc]]

for name, cap, sim in [("cf7", cf, cfs), ("d7", dd, ds)]:
    json.dump(cap, open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_{name}_cap.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    json.dump(sim, open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_{name}_sims.json"), "w"), indent=1)

sel = set()
for cap in (cf, dd):
    for v in cap.values():
        for lst in v[2]:
            if lst:
                sel.add(lst[0])
open(os.path.join(EXT, f"external_val_{SCALE}_grid_clips.txt"), "w").write("\n".join(sorted(sel)) + "\n")
print(SCALE, "queries", len(cf), "selected clips", len(sel))

# Adaptive context budgeting — oracle headroom, OOF gates, freeze decision

Date: 2026-11-20. Selection split: official val497 (FAITHFUL_V2, FULL corpus).
No test data was read in this analysis.

## 1. Oracle headroom (Gate G1–G3)

Per-query CIDEr over k ∈ {1,3,5,7} (fixed D ordering):

- k* distribution: k=1 336 (67.6%), k=3 80 (16.1%), k=5 43 (8.7%), k=7 38 (7.6%)
- 195/497 queries have identical output at all k; 302 are context-sensitive
- fixed best: D3 = 0.5312
- oracle adaptive: 0.5984
- **headroom = +6.71 CIDEr, 95% CI [+5.17, +8.47]**

Gate G3 (headroom ≥ +3.0) → adaptive budgeting is worth pursuing.

## 2. Predictability (diagnostic)

Best single features vs Δ(D3→D7): |Spearman| ≤ 0.06; AUC for "k=7 harm" ≤ 0.66
(`ground_coverage`, `repeat_sources7`). No inference-time feature reliably
predicts context harm, which caps what any simple selector can recover from the
oracle headroom.

## 3. 5-fold OOF (deterministic folds by video id)

| rule | OOF CIDEr | Δ vs D3 | 95% CI | mean k | folds > 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| similarity gap | **54.15** | **+1.03** | [−0.30, +2.52] | 2.30 | 5/5 |
| redundancy stop | 51.93 | −1.19 | [−3.36, +0.92] | 1.32 | 0/5 |
| quality-tail stop | 52.25 | −0.87 | [−2.85, +1.00] | 2.50 | 2/5 |
| saturation score | 51.99 | −1.13 | [−3.30, +0.86] | 1.62 | 1/5 |

Six metrics for the OOF gap rule: B1 79.88, B4 39.14, M 28.58, R-L 59.80,
CIDEr 54.21 (dataset-level), SPICE 7.80; mean k 2.30 (evidence −67% vs k=7).

## 4. Paired statistics of the frozen OOF selector

| Comparison | Δ CIDEr | 95% CI | p | W/L/T |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gap − D3 | +1.03 | [−0.30, +2.52] | 0.163 | 63/60/374 |
| gap − D1 | +2.41 | [+0.57, +4.49] | 0.016 | 55/42/400 |
| gap − D5 | +3.68 | [+1.71, +5.81] | 0.0002 | 103/73/321 |
| gap − D7 | +4.14 | [+1.74, +6.73] | 0.0008 | 123/97/277 |

## 5. Gate decision

- Strong gate (Δ ≥ +1.0 and CI excluding 0): **fails** (CI includes 0).
- Moderate gate (Δ ≥ +0.5 and ≥25% context-cost reduction, same direction in
  ≥4/5 folds): **passes** (+1.03; mean k 2.30 vs fixed 3/7; evidence −67%;
  5/5 folds positive).
- All purpose-built signals (redundancy, quality tail, saturation) **fail**.

**Frozen final method: similarity-gap adaptive context budget.**

Rule (no fitted parameters, inference-time only):
1. Score top-7 candidates with X-CLIP; take similarities s1..s7.
2. Compute adjacent gaps g_i = s_i − s_{i+1}, i = 1..6.
3. Budget = position of the largest gap mapped to {1,3,5,7}:
   i ≤ 1 → 1; i ∈ {2,3} → 3; i ∈ {4,5} → 5; i = 6 → 7.
4. Candidate order is the fixed ROUGE-L D ranking; only k changes.

`frozen_method_config.json` pins the rule, preprocessing and artifacts.

Caveat recorded for the paper: the selector is a generic baseline, not a novel
module; its val gain over D3 is not individually significant. The confirmatory
untouched-test comparison (frozen rule, no further tuning) decides whether it is
reported as the method or as a secondary finding next to fixed D3.

# N2 — VideoUFO ↔ MSR-VTT contamination audit

MSR-VTT: 10,000 videos (train/val/test) with `url` + start/end times in
`train_val_videodatainfo.json` / `test_videodatainfo.json`.

## 1. Source-level overlap (decisive)

VideoUFO clip IDs embed the YouTube source ID (`<yt_id>.<segment>`), and the CSV
carries segment start/end times. MSR-VTT metadata carries YouTube URLs and the
segment times.

| Split | MSR-VTT videos | same YouTube source in VideoUFO | same source AND ≥3 s time overlap |
|---|---|---|---|
| train | 6,513 | **0** | 0 |
| val | 497 | **0** | 0 |
| test | 2,990 | **0** | 0 |

Retrieved val497 top-7 candidates: 0 clips share a source ID with their query
video. **No video/source-level leakage exists.**

## 2. Caption text overlap

Exact normalized brief-caption intersection with VideoUFO's 812,014 unique
captions:

| Split | unique MSR-VTT captions | exact matches | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| train | 110,025 | 93 | 0.08% |
| val | 8,823 | 7 | 0.08% |
| test | 51,579 | 41 | 0.08% |

These are generic templates ("a man is talking", "a woman is walking") with no
source linkage; the 0.08% rate is identical across splits, i.e. baseline
vocabulary overlap rather than clip duplication.

## 3. Visual near-duplicate check

dHash (64-bit) on 3 frames per video; 497 val queries vs their 3,140 distinct
retrieved candidates:

- queries with any candidate at Hamming ≤ 6: **1/497**
- ≤ 10: 7/497
- random-corpus control mean min distance: 14.64

Manual inspection of the flagged queries shows graphics/static content
(Minecraft gameplay, cartoon cat on blue background, Cartoon Network logo,
dark cave scenes, website screenshots). dHash is unreliable on flat/graphical
frames; combined with the zero source-level overlap these are false positives,
not duplicated footage.

## Verdict

**No severe contamination.** No exclusion or experiment recomputation required.
This audit will be repeated for the final retrieved test candidates before
submission (same source-ID method, cheap and decisive).
